d: Install, onboarding, open an agent session, add a model, shortcuts
x: Nomi: One place. Every AI capability. Run Claude Code and Codex in parallel on one board. Connect a model once — official APIs, third-party, or local. No Nomi cloud account. No edits to those CLIs' global config. The desktop character is optional. Turn it off if you don't want it. # Install Download the installer for your system from GitHub Releases ( version is the Release version): System Installer macOS · Apple Silicon (M-series) Nomi- version -arm64.dmg macOS · Intel Nomi- version .dmg Windows 10+ (x64) Nomi-Setup- version .exe Linux (x64) Nomi- version .AppImage Linux (x64, Debian / Ubuntu) nomi_ version _amd64.deb Linux AppImage: chmod +x Nomi- version .AppImage ./Nomi- version .AppImage . The macOS build is signed but not notarized. If macOS says Nomi “is damaged”, move it into Applications, then run sudo xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Nomi.app . If Windows shows SmartScreen, click “More info → Run anyway”. # First-run onboarding On first launch the workbench-sized chat window opens with the guide covering the whole window. The three steps are language and look → AI (agents and a chat model) → personal ; the last two can be skipped. Skip from the corner. When it ends, Nomi opens the board if an agent is installed (the empty board's primary action is to dispatch Claude Code or Codex); otherwise it stays in chat and the sidebar's Get started card picks up from there. Rerun it later from Settings → General → Getting started guide → Reopen. AI · Agents : checks whether Claude Code and Codex are installed. Installed ones get a check mark; for the others, Install installs right away, as in Settings → Models Agents → Agents; a dialog appears only when something blocks the install, such as a missing Node.js or no write permission. Agents sign in with their own accounts, so dispatching them does not need a Nomi model. AI · Chat model (optional) : collapsed until you click Connect a model . Pick a third-party provider (a preset or a custom address), enter the key and check save; the model list stays greyed out until then, and the model you click becomes Nomi's chat model. Open full model settings ends the guide and jumps to Settings → Models Agents. You can dispatch agents without a model. Personal (optional) : name, occupation and interests. Whatever you fill in is saved when the guide ends, even if you skip it; untouched answers are left as they were. Occupation and interests drive the recommendations: the sidebar's Get started card suggests agents (Claude Code and Codex for developers, at least Codex for everyone else) and features (knowledge base, reminders, voice, importing MCP and skills), and the welcome screen's example questions change to match. Startup mode : the guide always opens the main window and keeps the desktop character off. If you want the desktop character, turn it on in Settings → General → Startup windows. Voice is not part of onboarding: the default is Edge online read-aloud (Xiaoyi, rate -5%) with Read AI replies aloud on; offline, Nomi just shows text. See Voice . # Connect a model Pick one: Cloud model : Settings → Models Agents → Third-Party Providers. Add a preset (e.g. DeepSeek, Kimi, OpenRouter) or a custom address, enter an API key and check save, then pick Nomi's chat model under Task Cost Routing. See Providers models . Local model : Ctrl/⌘+Shift+J (Settings → Models Agents → Local Models), download a recommended small model and start it; it registers as a provider automatically. See Local models . # Unified workspace direct CLI base All conversations and projects live in one unified sidebar. When local agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok, dsh, Kimi Code, MiniMax Code) are installed, agent sessions, endpoint filters, and the side workspace appear automatically. You can pick an installed official CLI directly per conversation inside main chat, or expand the multi-tab side workspace for Diff review, files, run traces, and a built-in terminal; see Agents . Terminal and IDE sessions on the Agent Board remain read-only. # Common shortcuts Shortcut Action Ctrl/⌘+K Command palette (search all actions settings) Ctrl/⌘+N New chat Ctrl/⌘+L Focus input Ctrl/⌘+, Open settings F2 (hold) Push-to-talk Full list and remapping: Personalization . # Tray menu From the system tray you can: open AI chat, switch the chat model, open model settings, open desktop abilities (file grants / activity log), trigger nomi's motions, open interaction settings (click-through / gravity / stroll), or quit.

d: Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI and more: accounts, providers, permission modes, side workspace, sessions
x: Screenshots are generated from the live UI driven by a mock CLI; chat content and paths are for demonstration only. Nomi's chat window can serve as a UI for local agents: messages, tool confirmations, permissions, and progress are forwarded to the real CLI, while reasoning and tool execution are handled by the CLI itself. Built-in support covers Claude Code , Codex , Grok , Gemini CLI , dsh , Kimi Code , MiniMax Code , and Antigravity CLI , and you can also connect any CLI that supports ACP (Agent Client Protocol). Select an endpoint from the sidebar's New conversation menu (or a project row's New button) to open an agent tab ( Ctrl/⌘+T ), or pick an installed official CLI directly per conversation inside main chat. Multiple sessions can run concurrently, and active sessions show a status dot at the start of their sidebar row. # Installation and Versions The left side of Settings → Models Agents → Agents lists each agent and its status (Not installed / Update available / version number): Each agent has a Version card for checking updates, one-click installation, and updating to the latest version. Installation and updates use your local Node.js and npm. Clicking runs the command immediately and streams logs in the card; logs collapse automatically and the version updates on success, or remain visible with the failure reason on error. A dialog is shown only if preflight checks fail (for example, Node.js is too old or the global npm directory is not writable). If the global directory lacks write permission, you can install to the user directory instead—Nomi never uses sudo . General checks the runtime environment (prompting with a download link if Node.js is missing, too old, or npm cannot be found) and hosts the Auto-approve All toggle (see below). # Official Accounts and Third-Party Providers Each tab selects its source from the composer's model/source chip, affecting only that tab: Official account : The CLI's own official sign-in. You can add multiple official accounts: each account gets an isolated config directory, sign-in goes through the CLI's official flow, and Nomi never stores login credentials. The default account is used for new tabs and tabs set to Follow default . dsh and Gemini CLI do not have Nomi-managed official accounts, so Default uses their own configuration: Gemini uses ~/.gemini from your terminal (API key, Vertex AI, or enterprise license; Google no longer allows Gemini CLI sign-in with personal Google accounts) or can switch to a third-party provider. Kimi Code and MiniMax Code sign in with Kimi / MiniMax accounts; if not signed in, the tab prompts you to sign in under Settings → Models Agents → Agents . Antigravity CLI ( agy ) supports signing in and out of its local official Google account inside the app, and does not support Nomi multi-account isolation or third-party gateway models. Third-party : Any model configured under Settings → Models Agents → Third-Party Providers , routed through Nomi's local gateway with automatic protocol translation. It applies only to the CLI process launched by Nomi and never modifies global configs such as ~/.claude , ~/.codex , ~/.grok , ~/.gemini , ~/.kimi-code , or ~/.minimax ; CLIs run directly in your terminal keep using your own configuration. When switching third-party models in Kimi Code or MiniMax Code, Nomi restarts the process and resumes the same session. Settings → Models Agents → Agents → Inherit terminal proxy : Routes login and chat traffic for all agents through the terminal https_proxy (localhost addresses and Nomi's own model requests bypass the proxy). Configured in one place rather than per agent. Choose the default source for new tabs under Settings → Models Agents → Agents → \ agent\ → New tab . Set each CLI's default third-party model under Settings → Models Agents → Task Cost Routing ; see Third-Party Providers Models . # Account Source and Launch Command For Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Kimi Code, and MiniMax Code, you can configure the account source individually under Settings → Agents → Assistants → \ agent\ → Account Launch : Use local sign-in : Sign in via the agent's own CLI first, and Nomi uses that existing account directly without adding it again, or creating, syncing, or injecting a Nomi account directory; model environment variables set in your terminal are also preserved. Multi-account managed by Nomi (default) : Add and select official accounts in Nomi, with an isolated config directory for each account. By default, Nomi uses the auto-detected CLI without requiring a command. When you need a wrapper script or network forwarder, enable Advanced: Custom launch command and enter the executable plus optional leading arguments, such as claude . Wrap paths containing spaces in double quotes. Nomi appends the driver's protocol, permission, model, MCP, and session-resume flags after your command; shell pipes, redirections, and variable expansion are not evaluated here, so use a wrapper script if needed. Account source and custom launch command take effect independently—disabling the custom command still preserves Use local sign-in , and selecting an account source does not enable a proxy on its own. dsh and Gemini do not currently have Nomi multi-account management and keep their existing third-party model configuration. All third-party models continue to use the existing gateway and launch behavior. Test launch appends only --version to the full command; it makes no model requests and does not validate accounts or network connectivity. After saving new settings, open idle official sessions carry over prior context into a new session on the next turn, and newly created sessions use the updated configuration immediately. Disabling the custom launch command does not delete the saved command or account data. Sign-in detection and subscription quota queries for Claude Code and Codex also use the custom launch command; when Use local sign-in is selected, Nomi does not inject its own isolated account directory. Quota availability depends on what the CLI returns; local token and cost records cannot be used to infer remaining subscription quota. # Permission Modes The permission mode in the input bar is set per tab (switch via /mode or Shift+Tab ) and unified into five levels mapped to each CLI's native flags: Level Meaning Plan Read-only; no file edits Ask each time Asks in a card before every change Auto-edit files Edits files automatically; confirms other actions Auto Runs most actions without asking Full access No confirmations; decided by the CLI CLIs that do not support a given level fall back to a safer one ( dsh only supports Plan / Auto-edit files / Full access; Kimi Code has no Auto-edit files; MiniMax Code only supports Plan / Ask each time; Antigravity CLI supports Plan / Ask each time / Auto-edit files / Auto). When confirmation is required, an Allow / Deny card appears in the chat; unanswered requests time out as denied after 2 minutes. When an agent needs input from you (Claude Code questions, Codex app-server prompts, or ACP forms), a unified question card appears above the input bar and is skipped if unanswered after 10 minutes. Auto-approve All ( Settings → Agents → Assistants → General , on by default): New regular agent tabs start in Full access , editing files and running commands without prompting; when turned off, new tabs start in the default mode and ask before each action. Only enable this in folders you trust. For regular background agent tabs launched by recurring tasks: when task authorization is set to L3 (risk-based auto-approval, on by default) and the system sandbox is active (macOS), together with Auto-approve All enabled in the foreground, command execution is handled by command review and approved without per-action prompts (on Windows and Linux without a system sandbox, regular background tasks still ask for each action; sandbox blocks and credential requests always prompt—see Schedules Tasks ). Agents delegated by Nomi in chat are not governed by this toggle; they run at the highest level supported by the target agent (usually Full access ) by default, with the effective level and applicable host protections shown in the approval card. # Local Protection Regardless of the permission level, Nomi enforces the following safeguards: System sandbox (macOS, on by default under Settings → Nomi → Desktop permissions → Privacy → Agent sandbox ): The agent runs inside a system sandbox that blocks reading sensitive locations (SSH and Git credentials, cloud credentials, keychains, browser data, personal data such as Mail / Messages / Photos, .env files, and private keys) and protected folders, and restricts writes to project folders plus its own config and cache. When blocked, a card appears in the chat (as well as in delegated sub-task cards and task details; the desktop character notifies you when the window is in the background) showing what the agent tried to read or write: Allow for this session (no further prompts in this session), Always allow (saved to settings, revocable under Privacy , scoped to this project only), or Don't allow (no further prompts in this session). Secret files such as .env are authorized per file, granting access only to the specific blocked file. Write access grants the narrowest possible scope (the containing folder or its Git repository); startup items, command directories (such as ~/.local/bin ), and shell configs (such as ~/.zshrc ) can never be authorized for writes. Granted permissions are preserved, and the next message launches and resumes the session with the updated permissions; approving does not automatically send a message or restart a stopped session. Agents are also informed they are running in a sandbox so they stop and explain blocks rather than working around them. When creating a background task, you can pre-check categories to Pre-allow in agent sandbox (GitHub outbound actions automatically include SSH and Git credentials) so the task runs without prompts. With the sandbox enabled, you can safely run agents with Auto-approve All . Other operating systems do not yet support the system sandbox; the remaining protections below still apply. Working directory : Must be a project folder. Root directories, the home directory, broad folders like Documents / Desktop / Downloads, system directories, built-in sensitive directories ( .ssh , .aws , etc.), and folders added under Settings → Nomi → Desktop permissions → Privacy are rejected. Directories are checked when selecting a folder, opening a new tab, and before every CLI launch; if settings change later, existing tabs with disallowed directories are blocked with an explanation. Environment variables : CLIs do not inherit tokens, passwords, cloud keys, or database connection strings from your environment (such as GITHUB_TOKEN , AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY , or DATABASE_URL ); model service credentials ( ANTHROPIC_* , OPENAI_* , etc., or cloud accounts when using Bedrock / Vertex) are passed as usual. Variables that are genuinely needed (such as NPM_TOKEN for private npm packages) can be added under Privacy → Allowed environment variables . Codex network access : Off by default; commands inside the sandbox cannot access the network. Under Auto-edit files , Codex sends a confirmation card before accessing the network or writing outside the workspace. Enabling Settings → Agents → Permissions → Let Codex use the network allows direct network access ( Full access is not subject to this restriction). When Nomi's system sandbox is enabled, Codex does not use its own sandbox and this setting has no effect. # Side Workspace and Session Layout Claude Code's local usage aggregation detects the actual config directory returned when the CLI launches, including isolated account directories used by custom launchers. After the first launch, it remembers the log path and continues scanning across restarts; the same message appearing in multiple directories is counted only once. Left : Unified session list (with project groups and endpoint filters) and Local history (past sessions recorded by each CLI, clickable to resume). Center : Conversation pane; click View changes or the title-bar toggle to expand the side workspace, or open files in the standalone file sidebar for focused reading. Right : Multi-tab side workspace ( Changes · Files · Split Terminal · Run Traces · Embedded Browser · Side Chat ), collapsed by default, with the change count shown on the top-bar toggle. All dividers can be dragged (positions are remembered) and double-clicked to reset. Select a project above the input box in a new session (with search and project creation); once the first message is sent, it is locked in. The working directory is the project's primary folder, and any additional folders in the project are also exposed to the agent for reading and writing ( --add-dir / writable directories for Claude Code and Codex, --include-directories for Gemini, and additionalDirectories for ACP assistants that advertise support; others operate only in the primary folder), with the system sandbox allowing those folders too. You can also switch branches there: click the branch name to search local branches, check one out, or Create and check out new branch . The branch selector at the top of the right-hand Changes pane controls the same switcher (disabled while an agent is running). If uncommitted changes would be overwritten, Git refuses the checkout so changes are not lost. If no project is selected, the working directory defaults to Documents/nomi (created on first use). # Changes and Git When the working directory is a Git repository, Changes reflects git status grouped into staged, unstaged, and untracked files, with an option to filter to files edited by the agent in the current session. The current branch and upstream branch appear at the top of the right pane. You can stage or unstage files directly, discard unstaged changes (saved to git stash so they can be recovered), enter a commit message and commit (or have an auxiliary model draft a commit message from the diff), undo unpushed commits, push, and pull (fast-forward only). Nomi never force-pushes and never pops up password prompts. Ask assistant to commit fills the commit instruction into the input box so you can confirm before sending it to the agent. Files lists the entire working directory (skipping dependency and cache folders such as node_modules and .next , and dimming .gitignore entries). Clicking a file opens the standalone sidebar with line navigation, source editing, and auto-save; Markdown files support an outline, rendered editing, and focus reading. Reads and writes reject symlinks pointing outside the working directory. When a project has multiple folders: Changes shows one section per Git repository (titled with the folder name, with the primary folder labeled and sections collapsible); branching, syncing, staging, and committing apply only to that section's repository. Multiple project folders inside the same repository are merged into one section, and non-Git folders are omitted from Changes . The badge count at the top is the sum across sections. Files shows one top-level node per folder, with the primary folder expanded by default. The full-screen review file tree is also grouped by folder. Typing @ in the input box suggests paths across all folders, displaying files from secondary folders as folder-name/path and inserting the absolute path. # Turn Edit Summary Card Whenever an agent edits files in a turn, an Edited N file(s) card appears under the message: you can expand inline line-by-line diffs, click View changes , open Full-screen review (listing all modified files sequentially alongside a file tree), or revert that turn's writes (with confirmation, scoped to the workspace). # Context Ring The ring indicator next to the input bar shows current context usage; hovering displays Current context xK / Max . Usage comes from the last model request in the current turn. Context window size prefers the value reported by the CLI and falls back to 128K for unrecognized models. /context uses the same accounting. # Sending Messages While Running You can keep typing while an agent is running: press Enter to inject into the current turn, Ctrl/⌘+Enter to queue until the current turn finishes, or Esc inside the input box to stop the run and send immediately. # Images Paste or drag images to send them to Claude Code, Codex, Grok, or Gemini; Nomi warns you if the current model does not support vision. dsh does not support images. # Session Management Switch model / reasoning effort : The model button in the tab's input bar switches only that tab. CLIs that support in-place switching apply the change without restarting; others restart and resume the same session. Inherit settings on new sessions : Each agent remembers the last selected permission mode, model, and reasoning effort ( Full access is not remembered). Hibernation : Tabs idle for an extended period (30 minutes by default) release their process and display Hibernated in the sidebar, resuming automatically on the next message. Fork : Selecting Fork… in the session menu or Fork from here at the end of any reply opens the same dialog: fork into a new session on the same endpoint or (when agents are installed) another endpoint, choose how many recent turns of context to include (All / Last 20, 10, 5, or 3 turns), and pick a target project. Forking from a specific reply carries messages only up to that reply and omits later messages; the original session is untouched. # Supported Agents Only built-in agents are supported; adding external CLIs is no longer available. External CLIs added in older versions are automatically removed on upgrade: their configurations are deleted, along with any tabs, sidebar sessions, and messages that used them. # Monitoring and Quotas Agents running in your terminal can also be monitored; see Agent Monitor . Official account subscription quotas and usage costs live under Settings → Usage analytics ; see Privacy Security . # Implementation Design and architecture: Agent Integration . Manifests (capability flags, permission levels, install methods): packages/cli-catalog/src/ cli /manifest.ts . Core: session orchestration apps/desktop-go/internal/core/cli/harness , Git operations internal/core/cli/gitops.go , install and updates internal/core/cli/cli_update_service.go , official accounts internal/core/cli/accounts ; session drivers internal/clisdk , per-CLI plugins internal/cliplugins/ cli . UI: packages/ai-chat/src/components/SessionWorkspace , ProvidersPage . Controlling local apps: When agent-desktop is installed ( Settings → Computer Use → Allow agents to use , on by default), Claude Code, Codex, and ACP agent sessions receive Nomi's nomi-computer MCP server; see Automation Desktop Capabilities . # Image Message Recovery Agent image messages are synced and persisted through the shared resource pipeline. Original images, Base64 payloads, or accessible file paths provided in history or live protocols are restored as images; image-only messages are preserved as well, while missing or broken images render a placeholder. User attachments support zooming, panning, and switching between images; agent-generated images show recorded generation metadata and expose edit or reference actions where supported by the resource. History parsing for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Grok, and dsh supports image recovery. Kimi and MiniMax recover images from generic ACP events and messages already saved by Nomi, as they do not currently have standalone history importers. Whether an original image can be restored depends on whether the source record retained the data and whether the file remains accessible.

d: Who is working, how far along, memory and CPU; the memory guard pauses and resumes
x: The Agent Board lists what is currently running: active Nomi chats answering a turn, Nomi background runs, agents dispatched by Nomi or opened directly by the user, and external agent sessions opened outside Nomi, complete with memory and CPU usage. While the Task Board answers where does this task stand? , the Agent Board answers who is running, how many resources are they using, and where are they stuck? —and the two link to each other. Core logic lives in apps/desktop-go/internal/core/fleet , exposed through the coding contract domain ( fleet.state , fleet.archive , and the fleet.changed event in packages/contract/src/app/coding.ts ), with handlers in internal/core/codinghandlers/fleet.go and wiring in fleet_wiring.go . The UI lives in packages/ai-chat/src/components/Fleet . # Entry Points Agents in the left navigation bar (alongside Tasks and Library) opens the full board page; the icon shows a badge for items needing your attention, the active count, and a load ring. The load indicator on the left side of the title bar (next to the sidebar collapse button) shows running count · total memory · system CPU . Click it to open a popover listing active items, or jump straight to the full board. When the sidebar is collapsed, the session title yields width to this indicator ( --cd-titlebar-lead-w ). # Management Scope Subject scope Allowed Actions Nomi itself (core process, commands it runs, local models) — Not shown as a card Active Nomi chat answering a turn managed Observe only Nomi background run (recurring task with executor nomi ) managed Pausable (task pause) CLI tabs in the orchestrator (chat delegations, task dispatches, direct user tabs) managed Pausable Agent sessions outside Nomi's process tree (started directly in a terminal or IDE) external Read-only; alerts only, never interfered with Scope is determined by process relationships rather than delegation flags: every tab in the orchestrator (including tabs you opened yourself or took over) counts as managed. External sessions are those discovered by agent monitoring ( internal/core/agents ) from local session files, excluding Nomi's own tab sessions: every session ID used by a tab is recorded ( agents/owned.go , persisted in owned-sessions.json ; IDs unseen for 30 days are pruned, and active IDs are flushed to disk at most once per hour based on last-seen time). Even after a tab closes, switches session ID on error, or restarts, sessions dispatched by Nomi will never reappear as Terminal · Read-only . External sessions are excluded from all control APIs; future pause, stop, or message-injection endpoints only accept managed IDs. In Mock CLI mode ( NOMI_USE_MOCK_CLI=1 , used for demo screenshots and E2E tests), OwnProcsOnly is enabled: processes outside Nomi's process tree are hidden from the board so real local agents and their directories never appear in screenshots. Active Nomi chats come from the chat router ( airouter.Handlers.ActiveChats ): streams carrying extra.conversationId (auxiliary calls such as title generation omit it). Titles are resolved by the UI from the session list. Idle Nomi chats do not appear under In progress . # Page Layout Header : Title, the Act automatically when memory is low toggle, and system memory pressure · physical memory · system CPU (background tint shifts under high load). Board : Status filters (All / To do / In progress / Paused / Done, with live counts), search by title / agent / directory, and filter by agent type. Cards are laid out in two columns (one column on narrow viewports), with items needing your input sorted first within each status. Each card shows the agent, status, title, source and directory, queue / pause / error reason, completion summary, time since last activity, and CPU / memory usage. Pause / Resume lives in the upper-right corner of the card; finished managed tabs show Close tab in the lower-right corner (with confirmation); actions to open the tab / task / chat or archive live in the ⋯ menu. Because the core does not report completion percentages, the status bar at the bottom of a card never fakes progress: In progress shows an animated accent strip, while Done shows a solid success bar. Below the header : The most recent memory governor action (within the last 10 minutes). Bottom bar : Scheduling policy (see below). Below the board : Idle process list. # Statuses There are only four statuses, with no historical log retained. Managed and external items share the board (external cards use a dashed border and have no action buttons): Status Sources To do ( todo ) Queued tabs; queued CLI tasks waiting to open a tab; queued Nomi background runs In progress ( running ) Actively running items; items waiting for approval ( needsYou: permission ), blocked by the sandbox ( sandbox ), or waiting on a question ( question , labeled Waiting for you ) also stay here Paused ( paused ) Frozen CLI tabs—paused automatically by the memory governor ( paused.by: memory ), manually by the user ( user ), or by Nomi ( nomi ); paused background runs Done ( done ) Finished tabs, background runs, and external sessions (an external session waiting for your reply means its turn finished, so it lands here); items awaiting acceptance ( needsYou: accept ) or errored ( failed ) To do cards state why execution hasn't started yet ( queueReason ): memory (held by the memory governor due to memory pressure), retry (waiting to retry after a failure, with retryAt ), or slot (waiting on earlier work because the concurrency cap, hourly launch cap, or orchestrator active-tab limit is full). Normally dispatched work starts immediately, so To do is usually empty. Never-run empty tabs, idle recurring tasks waiting for their next trigger, and idle external sessions are omitted from the board; external sessions marked as running whose process has exited are treated as Done . Finished items can be archived ( fleet.archive ): this only removes them from the board without touching the tab or session, and they reappear if they start running again; items still needing user action cannot be archived. Archive state is kept in memory only. Finished items with no activity for two hours are automatically hidden. # Resource Usage Process table ( internal/core/agents/proctable.go ) reads parent PID, resident memory, and cumulative CPU time for all processes in a single pass. On macOS it calls libproc and KERN_PROCARGS2 directly ( procnative_darwin.go , ~4 ms, no subprocesses); on Windows it uses a Toolhelp snapshot plus per-process GetProcessTimes , memory queries, and NtQueryInformationProcess for command lines ( procnative_windows.go ), falling back to ps or PowerShell Win32_Process when unavailable; on Linux it uses ps . Per-agent CPU is computed as the delta in cumulative CPU time across two samples divided by the elapsed interval ( 100 = one full core, matching Activity Monitor's % CPU column) rather than ps 's %cpu . The process list is shared across callers for 5 seconds ( agents.ProcessesShareTTL ): the board and agent progress monitor read on their own timers without spawning duplicate ps or PowerShell calls. When the progress monitor (runs every 8 seconds) finds no agent processes, it re-reads the process table at most once every 30 seconds ( agents.IdleProcsMs ) while continuing to scan session files every tick—so newly opened terminal agents appear within at most 30 seconds. System CPU ( system.cpuPercent , 0–100 across all cores, matching Activity Monitor's System + User total) reads OS counters ( agents.SystemCPU : host_statistics on macOS, /proc/stat on Linux, GetSystemTimes on Windows). When unavailable (such as non-cgo macOS builds), it falls back to summing process CPU divided by core count, which misses short-lived processes that exited between samples and kernel_task . Tab processes : The orchestrator records the spawned PID per tab in spawnCLI ( Orchestrator.TabPids ) and expands the full process tree from the process table; each PID is counted once. Nomi itself : Nomi's own process tree minus all tab process trees. Nomi chats and background runs execute inside the core process, so individual per-item usage is not available. External processes : Agent processes are grouped by process tree ( agents.AgentTrees , so an agent spawned inside another agent counts toward the same tree). Processes that register an active session (such as Claude Code's ~/.claude/sessions/ pid .json , agents.Service.ProcSessions ) map exclusively to that session; a newly opened process with no session file yet (no message sent) counts as idle instead of claiming an older session in the same directory. Remaining trees are claimed by external sessions matching the same agent type and working directory ( agents.Service.ProcCwds ), prioritizing running sessions. Unclaimed trees (open in a terminal or IDE with no active session) are placed in externalIdle.items , listed one per row under Idle processes below the board. # Closing Idle Processes Manually External sessions are strictly read-only, with one exception: you can manually close idle external processes ( fleet.closeIdle , dangerous ). Click Close on a row to stop one process, or check multiple rows (or select all) and click Close selected to batch-close them. After one confirmation, the UI invokes fleet.closeIdle for each item and lists a per-row reason for any that could not be closed. For each item, the core re-reads the process table to verify that the PID is still the root of an idle tree for the same agent type and not inside Nomi's process tree (if it started a session, exited, or had its PID reused, it returns FLEET_NOT_IDLE ), then sends SIGTERM to the tree (children first) and SIGKILL after 3 seconds if still alive. Verification only trusts a fresh process table read taken after the click: if reading fails (e.g., PowerShell timeout on Windows), it retries once and returns FLEET_CLOSE_UNVERIFIED without sending any signal—never verifying against a cached board snapshot. Neither the scheduler nor the memory governor ever invokes this. # Sampling Sampling happens on demand and is reused within 1 second. The UI polls fleet.state every 3 seconds while the board or popover is open, every 15 seconds otherwise, and stops polling when the window is hidden. fleet.changed is pushed whenever a tab, task, external session, or chat stream starts or ends. Known limitations: ps resident memory excludes compressed memory; Linux process CPU time has 1-second resolution; reading the process table once on Windows is relatively slow. # Scheduling Policy Defined in internal/core/fleet/policy.go . Sets the combined concurrency cap for agents dispatched by Nomi and background tasks. Users pick one of three presets at the bottom of the board ( fleet.setPolicy , persisted alongside the auto-manage toggle in fleet/settings.json ), taking effect immediately: Preset Concurrency Cap Save resources ( saver ) Up to 5 combined Balanced ( balanced ) Up to 10 combined (default) Full speed ( max ) Unlimited count: new work queues when memory pressure is elevated/critical or system CPU ≥ 85%, and starts automatically once load eases The concurrency limit spans both synchronous delegations and recurring tasks (including background delegations): both sides receive the cap ( delegate.SetMaxParallel / tasks.Runtime.SetMaxConcurrent ), count the other side's active runs when checking capacity ( SetSharedLoad , reading the peer's atomic counter without acquiring its lock), and trigger a queue re-evaluation on the other side whenever a slot frees up ( SetOnFreed ). Synchronous delegations and follow-ups triggered inside a background Nomi run do not queue; instead they borrow their parent task's slot ( delegate.borrowSlot , at most one child at a time per parent task, without double-counting), preventing deadlock when all slots are held by parent tasks waiting on child results (#294). Tabs opened directly by the user and external terminal/IDE sessions are not counted. Under the two fixed-cap presets, excess work queues ( queueReason: slot under To do ) rather than failing; lowering the cap does not interrupt running items, and raising it starts queued items immediately. Full speed holds work by resource state ( Holding , independent of the auto-manage toggle; system CPU is computed every 5 seconds by the memory governor from agents.SystemCPU counter deltas), setting queueReason to memory or cpu ; synchronous delegations in foreground chat return memory_pressure under this condition. The runaway safeguard limiting recurring tasks to at most 30 launches per hour applies regardless of preset. Preset names and values are supplied by the core in policy / policyOptions on fleet.state and rendered directly by the UI. # Memory Governor Defined in internal/core/fleet/governor.go . Reads system memory pressure every 5 seconds ( agents.SystemMemory : kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level and kern.memorystatus_level on macOS; MemAvailable and PSI on Linux; GlobalMemoryStatusEx on Windows with 15% free = warning and 7% free = critical) and acts only on managed CLI tabs—never touching external sessions. When the upper-right toggle ( Act automatically when memory is low , fleet.setAutoPause , persisted in userData/fleet/settings.json , on by default) is turned off, the governor stops acting automatically and resumes tabs it had paused; tabs paused by Nomi are not resumed and continue waiting for memory to recover. Pressure Action Warning or above Immediately reclaims CLI processes of tabs idle ≥ 1 minute ( Orchestrator.ReclaimIdleNow , sharing idle-reclaim rules; sessions stay intact, lossless); repeats once per minute while pressure persists Critical Freezes one running tab every 10 seconds: tabs dispatched by Nomi (chat delegations, tasks) before user-opened tabs, highest memory first within each tier; skips tabs resumed within the last 2 minutes and the tab the user is currently viewing (when the window is in the foreground) Normal and stable for 30s Resumes one tab paused by the memory governor or by Nomi every 20 seconds (oldest paused first); tabs manually paused by the user are never auto-resumed Freezing sends SIGSTOP / NtSuspendProcess ( Orchestrator.FreezeTab , with the process tree expanded from the process table, parent first): the process uses zero CPU and its memory can be compressed or paged out by the OS. On resume ( ThawTab , children first), the current turn picks up seamlessly where it left off, invisible to delegations and recurring tasks. Because frozen processes cannot handle interrupts or accept input, the orchestrator always thaws them before stopping, closing, sending messages, injecting input, approving prompts, or tearing down processes, and thaws all frozen tabs on exit ( Dispose ). Cards also expose manual Pause / Resume buttons ( fleet.pause / fleet.resume ). The line below the board header shows the most recent governor action within the last 10 minutes. Nomi chats and background Nomi runs execute inside the core process and cannot be frozen. Pause / Resume on background runs maps to task pause ( fleet.pause / fleet.resume translates run: taskId into task pause / resume commands through the same tasks.Service.Command entry point as the Task Board): scheduling stops, the in-flight turn finishes (the card stays in In progress labeled Pauses after this turn ), and the run then moves to Paused without starting new turns until resumed by the user or resume_agent ; memory recovery never auto-resumes it and the memory governor does not touch it. Only running or queued runs that are not waiting on user input can be paused; active foreground chats are observe-only; runs stopped automatically after consecutive failures do not count as paused and do not appear on the board. Who paused an item ( user / nomi ) is held only in the board service's memory and resets to user across restarts. # Nomi Dispatching Tools ( internal/core/fleet/tools.go , registered in Nomi's tool table and exposed only when the conversation touches agents, memory, slowdowns, pausing, or dispatched work): list_agents (reports pressure, free percentage, system CPU, Nomi's own usage, and all agents, marking external ones readOnly ) and pause_agent / resume_agent (only for managed, pausable items; rejects external sessions, active foreground chats, and items waiting on user input with an explanation). Agents paused by Nomi ( paused.by: nomi ) behave like governor-paused tabs and auto-resume once memory returns to normal so they are never stranded; background runs paused by Nomi wait for manual resume. Admission control : When memory is critical and auto-management is enabled, the memory governor holds back new work. The task runtime checks Admit ( tasks.Runtime.SetAdmit ) before starting execution, keeping agent tasks and background Nomi tasks in the queue ( queueReason: memory under To do ) while notification-only tasks proceed normally; once pressure clears, the queue is re-evaluated immediately ( OnRelease → Runtime.Tick ). For synchronous delegations, background Nomi runs wait for pressure to ease, while foreground chats receive memory_pressure so Nomi can switch to background delegation. The dispatching prompt also instructs Nomi to call list_agents first when the system feels sluggish or before dispatching multiple agents at once. Dispatch tree : Background Nomi runs carry their task ID on the context ( tasks.WithRunTask ). Any agent tab delegated from that run records parentTaskId , and its board card displays Dispatched by … ( parentId ). # Threading fleet.* avoids entering the JS runtime GIL unnecessarily: recurring tasks' Runtime.List is read outside the GIL (the runtime holder might be waiting on the GIL), and jsrt.Call enters the GIL only when reading tabs and agent monitor state. Chat router stream start/end notifications run on a separate goroutine so they never block the stream.

d: Progress notices for local coding tools
x: Nomi can watch agents running locally on your machine (including sessions launched directly in a terminal) and notify you once when a task finishes, fails, or completes a turn and is waiting for your reply—without broadcasting mid-turn progress. When multiple agents finish or fail within 1.5 seconds of each other, Nomi combines them into a single notification instead of interrupting repeatedly; prompts waiting for your action are never merged and pop up immediately. Sessions managed in Nomi's own agent tabs notify only once on the tab side. Idle session files touched by a CLI during exit or cleanup do not trigger another completion alert, and an initial environment stub created by Gemini before you have sent a message is not counted as a session. Location: Settings → Agents → Monitor sessions . Here you'll find the master Watch agent progress toggle, per-agent toggles, detected tools, Scan now , and the active session list (Nomi's own agent tabs can be opened directly from the list). Notification style and types are configured under Settings → General → Notifications / Dynamic Island , and Do Not Disturb hours live under Schedules . # Supported Tools Claude Code, Codex, dsh , Grok, Gemini CLI, Kimi Code, and MiniMax Code—each can be toggled on or off individually. # Statuses In progress : Session file was recently written to and the process is still running. Waiting for you : The current turn has finished and the process is still running. May be stuck : The process is still running, but there have been no updates for an extended period (5 minutes by default; shown in the list only, with no notification). Done / Failed / Ended . Sessions are deduplicated by session ID; historical sessions discovered for the first time never trigger notifications—alerts fire only on status transitions. # When Notifications Fire Notify once at completion : Starting, in-progress, and potentially stuck states are shown only in the list with no alert or speech; completion, failure, and waiting-for-reply trigger a single notification, while confirmation requests trigger immediately. The legacy 10-minute periodic summary ( N coding tasks still in progress ) and its timer have been removed; there are no mid-run progress broadcasts. Read aloud (off by default): When enabled, reads the outcome aloud in addition to playing the notification sound, respecting the voice toggle and mute state. When the Nomi workbench is visible on screen, completion alerts do not pop up the Dynamic Island—only confirmation-needed and failure alerts do—and the tab you are currently viewing suppresses all popups (see Dynamic Island ). When Nomi is visible on the desktop, notifications appear in her speech bubble; otherwise they use the Dynamic Island , falling back to system notifications if the Dynamic Island is unavailable. # Principles Nomi only reads session and log files already written locally by these tools and checks whether the corresponding processes are running; it never signs in or accesses any remote accounts. # Implementation apps/desktop-go/internal/core/agents : process detection processes.go , session scanning fsscan.go , per-tool session parsers parsers.go , defaults settings.go . Grok status is inferred solely from file modification times and process presence. UI: packages/ai-chat/src/components/CodingMonitor .

d: The / palette; built-ins run in the UI, the rest go to the CLI
h: Built-in Commands (Local Execution, Zero Model Turns)
x: Type / in the input box of any session (Nomi chat or an agent tab) to open the command palette. Once selected, commands run inside Nomi's UI and render their output as cards in the conversation stream . # Usage Action Behavior Type / Opens the palette; keep typing for fuzzy search ( /cnt matches /context ) ↑ ↓ Select a command Enter Execute; commands taking arguments (shown with argument hints in the palette) complete to / name first so you can enter arguments and press Enter again Tab Autocomplete only without executing Esc Close the palette //xxx Send a literal /xxx (not treated as a command) Paths such as /usr/bin Sent as plain text Commands are grouped in order: current endpoint (the CLI's own commands), project custom commands, user custom commands, plugins, Skills, and finally Nomi built-in commands. The badge on the right of each entry indicates who handles it: Built-in , Forwarded to CLI , Expanded (Nomi reads and expands the command file before sending), or Unsupported . When a session has a working directory, typing @ autocompletes file paths inside it. # Built-in Commands (Local Execution, Zero Model Turns) /context : Context window usage with a progress bar and category breakdown. Total usage matches Claude Code / Codex accounting: input tokens (including cache reads and writes) plus output tokens from the last model request, labeled Actual when real usage data is available or Estimated otherwise; unrecognized models default to 128K. In Nomi chats, the breakdown separates system prompt, tool definitions, long-term memory, and message categories: the core estimates ratios from the actual outbound request, then calibrates using the first request's real input and the delta between the last and first requests so the parts sum to the total. In Grok tabs, /context is forwarded to Grok itself. /cost ( /usage , /stats ): Token and cost totals for this session, today, and the last 7 days from the local usage ledger. /status : Endpoint, model / provider, working directory, sign-in method, CLI version, and session. /model [name] : Lists available models and switches; /model name switches directly. /mode : Cycles permission modes (Plan / Ask each time / Auto-edit files / Auto / Full access), same as Shift+Tab . /clear ( /new , /reset ): Starts a new conversation while keeping the previous one in history. /diff : Uncommitted changes in the current working directory (relative to HEAD , including untracked files). /plugins ( /skills , /mcp , /agents ): Opens the read-only Plugin Panel. /help : Available commands and execution modes for the current endpoint. Available only in Nomi chats: /agent name [request] : Explicitly delegates to a specific agent (running in the background by default), such as /agent codex fix the login bug . When a request is provided, it dispatches immediately without going through the chat model; if the agent is not installed, delegation is disabled, or dispatch fails, Nomi explains why in chat instead of claiming it succeeded. Entering only the name routes the next message to that agent, and /agent off cancels. Typing / shows /agent among built-in commands; typing /agent lists available agents (installed ones first, uninstalled ones dimmed). See AI Chat . /compact [focus] : Summarizes earlier turns to free up context space (also runs automatically before sending when nearing the limit); any focus text you provide is prioritized in the summary. Enabled Nomi skills (see MCP Skills ) also appear as / skill-name and follow the skill instructions when selected. # Forwarded and Expanded Commands Claude Code : /compact , /init , /code-review , /security-review , /effort , /config , and similar commands are forwarded verbatim to the CLI; project and user custom commands and skills in .claude/commands and .claude/skills are also listed and forwarded verbatim. Codex : /compact is forwarded to Codex to compact the current session; project and user skills are expanded by Nomi ( $ARGUMENTS , $1 , …) and sent as a user message. Grok : Commands supported by Grok's headless mode (such as /compact and /context ) and skills are forwarded verbatim to Grok. Gemini, dsh : Nomi built-in commands only. # Unsupported and Unknown Commands Native CLI commands that cannot work under the current integration mode (such as /memory , /permissions , /login , and /resume ) are omitted from the menu; typing their full name explains why they are unsupported and what to use instead. Typing a nonexistent /xxx never sends it to the model —Nomi flags it as an unknown command and offers Send as plain text . # Plugin Panel (Read-Only) In agent tabs, open it from the + menu in the input bar ( Plugins / Commands ) or via /plugins : lists discovered commands, Skills, plugins, MCP servers (names and transport types only), and subagents for the current endpoint. In Nomi chats, /plugins displays Nomi's own skills and MCP servers (managed under Extensions ). There are no toggles in the panel: Nomi does not modify individual CLI configurations on your behalf. # Privacy and Security Command discovery reads only filenames and file headers (the first 8 KB of each file), and never reads credential or settings files ( auth.json , .credentials* , .env* , settings*.json , config.toml , ~/.claude.json ); from .mcp.json , only server names and transport types are extracted. Symlinks are checked against their resolved real path. Command files are expanded by the core by ID—the UI cannot pass arbitrary paths—and dynamic shell injection ( !`cmd` ) inside command files is never executed by Nomi. # Implementation UI: packages/ai-chat/src/slash ( registry.ts , adapters/ endpoint .ts , atPathComplete.ts ), components/SlashPalette , components/PluginPanel . Core: command discovery apps/desktop-go/internal/core/cli/slashdiscovery.go .

d: Data location, local-only mode, outbound masking, prompts, export
x: Nomi is local-first: your data stays on your computer. Location: Settings → Privacy permissions , organized into three tabs: Privacy data , Outbound protection , and Data export . File authorizations, tool permissions, and action logs live under Settings → Nomi → Desktop permissions . # Where Data Is Stored Chats, memories, knowledge base indexes, reminders, schedules, tasks, skills, and settings are all stored in the local app data directory (referred to below as userData ), never uploaded or synced: OS Path macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Nomi Windows %APPDATA%\Nomi Linux ~/.config/Nomi (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Nomi ) Chat transcripts live in userData/conversations/ (see AI Chat ) with 0600 file permissions. API keys, cloud recognition keys, and MCP secrets/tokens are encrypted via the OS secure credential store. If the OS credential store is unavailable, Nomi refuses to save them rather than falling back to plaintext on disk. # Local-Only Mode Only local models can read files under Settings → Nomi → Desktop permissions → Cloud local-only : when enabled, file contents, images, knowledge base snippets, and audio recordings are sent only to local models (such as Ollama or the built-in llama.cpp ); requests carrying this content to cloud models are rejected. When disabled, each cloud model prompts for your consent the first time it is about to receive such content, and consented models are listed on the same page. Offline mode on the Local models page also turns this setting on. If you switch models mid-conversation, previously read files, command outputs, and web pages are re-evaluated against the new model, and disallowed items are replaced with placeholders before sending. Paginated reads of previously truncated outputs and summarization models handling earlier steps in long-running tasks are likewise re-checked against the actual receiving model: disallowed paginated reads are blocked, and disallowed items in summarization inputs are replaced with placeholders. # Outbound Protection Settings → Privacy permissions → Outbound protection (on by default): before sending requests to third-party providers, secrets in messages, file contents, and command outputs are replaced with placeholders and restored in the reply, keeping the original secret strictly on your machine. Applies to both Nomi chats and all agents. Detects provider API keys, tokens (GitHub, Slack, JWT, etc.), private keys (PEM), and passwords (connection strings, assignments); Strict detection also matches by key name (which may produce false positives). When a secret is detected, you can choose Redact (default), Warn only (send as-is and log an entry), or Block (abort the turn). Send format-matched fake keys : Substitutes a synthetic key matching the prefix, length, and character classes of the real one so format validation checks still pass. Registered secrets : For values without a standard format—such as internal company tokens or database passwords—register them (at least 8 characters, stored encrypted locally) to hide them in every outbound request; use Never redact for false positives. Also hide for local models is off by default, since traffic to local or LAN models such as Ollama and LM Studio never leaves your machine/network. Try it lets you paste text and preview locally what a provider would receive; Recently hidden secrets logs only the type, length, and leading characters. # Permissions and Confirmations Files can only be accessed inside folders you have authorized (via the system folder picker or by clicking Authorize on a Request folder access card in chat). Sensitive locations are always denied, and you can add extra protected folders under Desktop permissions → Privacy . See Automation Desktop Capabilities . Local protection for agents : Agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) can only operate inside project folders—root directories, your home directory, broad folders like Documents or Desktop, system directories, and protected folders are disallowed. Neither agents nor Nomi's workspace commands inherit tokens, passwords, cloud keys, or database connection strings from your environment (model service credentials are still passed, and genuinely needed variables can be allowlisted under Privacy ). Codex disables network access by default and asks before going online. On macOS, agents also run inside a system sandbox (on by default) that blocks reading sensitive paths and restricts writes to project folders; blocked attempts can be authorized per session or permanently in chat. See Agents . Projects for Nomi chats : Above the input box of a new chat, you can attach a project to each Nomi conversation (or leave it unset). Nomi's file tools work directly across all folders in the project, and commands start in the primary folder. Outside the project, only folders and files you separately authorized (including files dropped onto Nomi) are accessible, following normal authorization and confirmation rules. Your home directory itself, its parents, Documents / Desktop / Downloads themselves, system directories, and sensitive directories cannot be added to a project, nor can one folder in a project contain another. If a folder is later deleted or added to the protected list, Nomi and agents stop using it (if the primary folder becomes unusable, the whole project becomes unavailable). No confirmation for workspace file operations ( Settings → Nomi → Permissions handoff , follows Auto-approve All unless explicitly overridden): When enabled, file reads and writes inside project folders no longer prompt individually; unauthorized paths outside the project and sensitive files remain blocked. Auto-review commands ( Settings → Nomi → Permissions handoff , on by default): Under Auto-edit files , Nomi sends commands ( workspace_run ) to an auxiliary model for risk assessment before running them: low-risk commands run immediately, while high-risk commands—or any command in a turn that has read untrusted external content (web pages, command outputs, clipboard, knowledge base, MCP responses, delegated agent results, etc.; files in the workspace or authorized folders do not count)—prompt you for confirmation. Switching to Auto runs allowed commands directly without a confirmation card. If the review fails or times out, or if the auxiliary model is in the cloud and you have not consented to sending content to it, Nomi falls back to asking you. When turned off, every command asks for confirmation. Under Auto-edit files , commands still prompt if external content was read, if the review flags risk, or if review is unavailable. Note: commands run as your user account and are not confined to the workspace —they can read and write anything you have access to. Command allowlist : Checking Don't ask again for commands starting with this on a command confirmation card records its prefix (such as pnpm test , go test , git status , pnpm run build ) in the allowlist so matching commands run directly without review or prompts. Only recognized test, build, lint, or read-only inspection program subcommand pairs (such as pnpm test , go vet , cargo check , make test , git diff , tsc ) are eligible—bare program names (such as make ) are not. Only simple commands can be saved: pipes, redirections, ; / chaining (except a single leading cd subdir ), and command substitutions are ineligible. Commands containing flags that swap binaries or write to arbitrary paths ( -exec , -toolexec , -vettool , --output , -O , --config ) are neither saved nor auto-approved (evaluated on post-unquoting shell arguments, catching forms like -exec=… and --out put =… , as well as unambiguous long-option prefixes such as --outp=… ). Review and confirmation still apply when: external content was read in the current turn; files were modified in a turn that read external content (subsequent turns in that conversation are also paused until you manually confirm one command in that conversation, for up to 24 hours; other conversations are unaffected); the mode is Ask each time ; or you set that tool individually to Always ask . View or remove rules under Desktop permissions → Tool permissions → Command allowlist ; older saved rules that no longer qualify are dropped automatically. The permission mode in Nomi chat's input bar ( Shift+Tab to cycle) controls how often Nomi's own tools ask: Plan : Read-only; mutating actions are rejected immediately. Ask each time : Prompts on every change, with no don't ask again in this chat option. Auto-edit files (default): Follows each tool's setting under Desktop permissions → Tool permissions . Auto : Runs allowed tool calls directly without per-action prompts; workspace boundaries, sensitive paths, and OS-level extra consents still follow their respective rules. Destructive actions and writes after reading external content in the same turn also run directly at this level; switch back to Auto-edit files or Ask each time when tighter control is needed. Per-conversation approval : Clicking Always allow on a confirmation card for mutating actions (or the matching confirmation on the Dynamic Island) suppresses further prompts for the same action category in that conversation (file edits form one category, delegations and follow-ups another, desktop control another, and all other tools are scoped per tool). The button tooltip states the exact scope, and reading external content will not re-trigger prompts within it; switching to another conversation requires fresh approval, and approvals clear on app restart. Deletions and other destructive actions, command execution (governed by the command allowlist), Ask each time mode, and tools configured as Always ask (such as browser actions) are excluded from per-conversation approval. Desktop control is an exception: clicking Allow covers all subsequent desktop actions in that conversation—including payments, sending, deleting, and coordinate clicks—while Always allow on the card auto-approves across all future conversations. Password managers, banking apps, and Nomi's own windows remain blocked. Emergency stop and audit logging continue to apply. No re-confirmation for follow-ups : Once a delegation is approved, subsequent follow-ups sent by Nomi to the same agent do not re-prompt each time ( Plan still blocks them and Ask each time still prompts). Every tool call is recorded in the local audit log (logging only argument hashes and lengths). For agent permissions, see Agents : when Auto-approve All is enabled, new tabs run with Full access and their commands can access anything you can access. # Export and Clearing Data export : Bundles selected categories ( conversations/ , long-term memory, schedules and reminders, skills, settings) into a .zip archive; excludes API keys and encrypted MCP configuration values. Under Privacy data , you can clear the current conversation (deleting only messages in that chat), manage memories, or jump to usage privacy settings; memories, desktop permissions, and other stores can also be cleared individually. Generate chat titles with model : When enabled, the first message of a new chat is sent once more to the active model to generate a title; when off, the first sentence is used directly. # Subscription Quotas and Sign-In Credentials Settings → Usage analytics → Usage cost displays official account subscription quotas per tool (Claude Code, Codex, Grok), with a refresh button on each card. Quota bars are shown only for account/subscription sign-ins; API-key or third-party-provider setups show API billing, no subscription quota while still tracking usage and cost. Nomi never touches sign-in credentials : It never reads, stores, or uploads auth.json , .credentials.json , or OS keychain entries, never calls undocumented endpoints, and never estimates quotas. Quotas come from only two sources : Data already present locally (such as quota snapshots written to session logs by Codex, or quota data in Claude Code's status-line input—the latter requires opting in on the card), plus results fetched using the official CLI's own login session when you manually refresh (temporarily running claude -p /usage , codex app-server , or Grok ACP in read-only, non-approving mode and exiting immediately). Nomi retains only percentage, window, reset time, and plan name; email addresses and account IDs are discarded. When multiple official accounts exist, these commands run inside the default account's own config directory. When Actively refresh quotas is turned off, refreshing only re-reads existing local data without launching any CLI. # Coding Tool Usage Logs Usage cost reads accounting fields already written locally by coding tools (timestamp, model, token counts, session/project name), deduplicates requests, and computes costs locally. Supports Claude Code, Codex, dsh , Grok, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot CLI, Kimi, and Aider. Read-only, accounting fields only: never reads message bodies or credentials; OpenCode and Copilot CLI SQLite databases are opened read-only and run fixed queries. Offline and never uploaded; respects each tool's home directory environment variables (such as CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR , CODEX_HOME , GROK_HOME ). Usage ledger : Deduplicated records are stored under userData/usage/ and pruned according to your Usage retention setting (1 year by default). Roughly the most recent 2 months live in ledger.jsonl and stay in memory per record; older entries are moved by local date into ledger-days/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl , keeping only daily totals and deduplication key hashes in memory ( ledger-days/index.gob caches those totals and is rebuilt if deleted). Charts and heatmaps read the daily totals directly, loading individual daily files only when request details or CSV exports query older dates. When re-scanning coding tool logs older than 2 months, only the corresponding day's file is opened to match gateway route records so the same request is never double-counted. After editing prices or adding custom pricing, costs for older dates are recalculated in the background—showing the previous cost until finished (token and call counts are unaffected). Downgrading to a version prior to 2.3.0 only displays the last ~2 months while leaving daily files intact, so upgrading back restores everything. Pricing and model metadata : Fetches the public pricing table and model parameters from https://models.dev/api.json (at most once every 12 hours on startup unless triggered via Sync now , and can be disabled); requests carry no usage or account data. Pricing precedence: custom synced built-in. # Diagnostic Logs Settings → Privacy permissions → Privacy data → Diagnostic logs helps troubleshoot third-party providers, agents, and gateway issues. Enabled by default (always on in development builds), allowing you to view raw gateway request bodies in a chat's Execution trace . Because this records conversation content and code locally, turn off Save diagnostic logs if you prefer not to keep them; your choice takes effect immediately for subsequent turns. When enabled by default, logs stay at normal verbosity; debug verbosity is enabled only when explicitly turned on in settings (or in development builds). Records raw agent I/O ( userData/logs/ , retained for 7 days) and gateway request/response bodies ( userData/gateway/trace/ , retained for 24 hours, pruning oldest files once total size exceeds 256 MB). Each gateway request has a trace ID included in the x-nomi-trace-id response header and in Requests . Keys, tokens, and Authorization headers are redacted; environment variables are never logged. Export diagnostics bundle packages the last 24 hours of logs into a .zip and runs a second redaction pass before export. Because the bundle contains chat content and code, share it only with people you trust. During development, set NOMI_DIAG_BODY=0 to disable gateway body tracing independently. # Application Security Communication between the UI and core occurs exclusively over a local 127.0.0.1 connection using a per-window one-time token and origin validation; every callable UI action is explicitly declared in the application contract. Nomi's speech bubbles and the Dynamic Island render plain text only. Before contacting external URLs, Nomi validates and blocks localhost, LAN, and other internal addresses (including obfuscated notations and post-DNS-resolution targets); local or LAN model endpoints require explicit confirmation. # Implementation Security Boundaries , Application Contract . Core: desktop permissions apps/desktop-go/internal/core/desktop , outbound protection internal/gateway/privacy , usage and quotas internal/core/usage , diagnostics internal/core/diagnostics , data export internal/core/local/hub.go , window tokens internal/contract/websocket.go . UI: packages/ai-chat/src/components/SettingsView ( PrivacySection.tsx , PrivacyModeSettings.tsx , DiagnosticsSettings.tsx ), DesktopPanel .

d: Assign models to chat and each agent, multiple keys, no model switch on failure
x: Entry point: Settings → Models Agents → Third-Party Providers (with Task Cost Routing in the first tab). Both Nomi chat and agents using third-party models connect through the local unified gateway, which handles protocol translation automatically. Circuit breaker failover at the top right is off by default; enable it if you want automatic failover across providers. # Switching Models The model picker in the chat area (grouped by provider, showing reasoning / vision / context length), the tray Chat model menu, and /model all update the same assignment and take effect on the next request. # Adding a Third-Party Provider No protocol selection is needed: Choose a source : Search presets (model vendors, relay platforms, and local services such as DeepSeek, Kimi, Zhipu GLM, Qwen, MiniMax, OpenRouter, OpenCode Go, Ollama, LM Studio) or choose Custom URL . Enter credentials : You can paste multiple keys at once (one per line; the first is the primary key and the rest act as fallbacks in order). For a custom URL, you can paste the base URL, /v1 , or the full /v1/chat/completions path. If the service does not expose a model list, enter a model ID for testing. Probe and save : Nomi probes four protocols in parallel—Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Responses, Chat Completions, and Gemini—showing the result and failure reason for each. At least one protocol must succeed before saving. Fetched models have preset-recommended ones enabled by default; non-chat models (embeddings, audio, etc.) are listed but disabled. Local or LAN addresses (Ollama, self-hosted services) require confirmation before Nomi connects: local service presets are auto-confirmed, while custom URLs prompt for confirmation. # Adding from the Web Third-party providers that support Nomi links can be added directly from their website: One-click import : Click Add to Nomi ( nomi://provider/import link) on the provider's website. Nomi opens a confirmation dialog displaying the name, per-protocol URLs, masked key, and model count; it only saves after you click Add . Web authorization : Click Connect Nomi ( nomi://provider/connect ) on the provider's website, or click Web authorization on the Third-party providers page and enter its URL. After confirmation, your browser opens its authorization page; once you sign in and approve, return to Nomi to confirm once more. Nomi exchanges the key directly with the third-party provider so the key never appears in the link. Links may only carry public https URLs. If a third-party provider with the same URL already exists, confirming updates it rather than creating a duplicate. Up to 5 pending links can wait for confirmation, expiring after 10 minutes. Only add third-party providers you trust, as requests routed through them carry your conversation content. See Provider Link Integration for integration details. # Assignments Configure which model is used where under Assignments : Nomi : Chat, tool calling, summarization (the latter two default to Follow chat ), and image generation (defaults to Auto , picking an image model from the same vendor as the chat model). Agents : The default model each CLI uses when set to Third-party , plus the helper model (for generating titles, writing summaries, etc.; matches the main model if unset). For Claude Code, you can also expand Tier models to set Opus / Sonnet / Haiku / Fable tiers and the subagent model (Haiku tier is used for background tasks). # Multi-Key, Reconnect, and Fallback Each provider can have one primary key and multiple fallback keys; the UI displays masked values only. On transient upstream errors ( 408 , 429 , 5xx , timeouts, connection failures), Nomi retries with backoff on the same key first (starting at 0.5s, up to 8s, or honoring the upstream Retry-After duration)—up to 3 attempts per key, or 5 attempts when there is only one key—before moving to the next key. Invalid keys ( 401 / 403 ) switch to the next key immediately. After 10 cumulative failures on one provider, Nomi falls back to the next provider that offers the same model . It never silently substitutes a different model; if no other provider offers that model, an error is returned. When a local or LAN provider fails, it only falls back to other local or LAN providers and never sends requests to the cloud. Once a response has started streaming output, retries stop to avoid stitching a single reply from two separate requests. You can drag to reorder the provider list (keyboard: Alt+↑/↓ on the drag handle); providers higher in the list have priority. Each row has a toggle to disable or enable it directly. # Editing a Provider Click a row to open its details: Keys : Reorder (which sets fallback order), disable, rename, delete, or append keys. Each key shows its latest error, which clears automatically once it recovers. Models : Check to enable, add a model ID manually, or click Refresh to re-fetch (new models default to disabled). You can search and filter; Enable all / Disable all applies only to the currently filtered models. Advanced : Per-protocol URLs (leave blank to disable), restricting a model or key to a specific protocol, model mapping, custom headers and User-Agent , and clearing auto-learned state. Each key supports a concurrency limit and requests-per-minute limit (excess requests queue), plus a private note (account name, balance, expiration, up to 200 characters—visible only to you and never sent to the provider), shown truncated next to the masked key. Request body limit defaults to 32 MiB and can be adjusted from 1 to 256 MiB. Known model to treat as : Assigning a known model ( like ) to a model lets Nomi derive its capabilities and usage pricing from that known model. When a model mapping is configured (public name → upstream name), usage logs record the actual name sent upstream while pricing uses the like set on the public name. If multiple public names map to the same upstream name with conflicting like settings, Nomi does not guess and marks usage as unpriced. # Automatic Parameter Adaptation Based on the built-in model catalog (from models.dev ) and model-family rules, the gateway adapts requests into what the upstream model accepts: clamping out-of-range reasoning effort to the nearest supported level, handling unsupported sampling parameters, max_tokens formatting, and reasoning-content passback per model, and replacing images with a one-line note for models without vision support. When an upstream explicitly rejects a parameter, the gateway retries once with an alternate form and remembers the result. Every adjustment is noted under Usage analytics → Requests . Strict mode (toggle next to Show APIs on the Third-party providers page, off by default): When enabled, unsupported parameters fail immediately instead of being adapted, which is useful for diagnosing why a parameter did not take effect. # Agents Using Third-Party Models Each agent tab chooses Official account or Third-party in the top-right of the chat area. This applies only to that tab; see Agents . Third-party configuration applies only to the CLI process launched by Nomi—it never modifies any CLI's global config or touches official credentials. Session history is still written to each CLI's own directory as usual. When starting a third-party session, Nomi passes the model's actual context window and output limit to the CLI to avoid premature compaction or overflow errors. When switching a third-party tab back to an official account, third-party reasoning content cannot be sent to official endpoints, so Nomi continues in a new session with context carried over while keeping the original session intact. Each third-party tab's CLI process accesses the gateway with its own one-time token (passed only in that process's environment; the gateway stores only the hash), which is invalidated immediately when the process exits or the tab closes. Official tabs never carry a token. MiniMax Code's custom provider only reads keys written to its config file, so its token is written to a tab-private config file (readable only by you, permissions 600 ) that is also invalidated when the tab closes. # Terminal Launch Commands Toggle at the bottom of the Third-party providers page (off by default). When enabled, Nomi generates nomi-claude , nomi-codex , nomi-gemini , nomi-grok , and nomi-dsh in ~/.nomi/bin/ : running them in a terminal uses the third-party model assigned to that CLI under Assignments , and --nomi-model provider/model overrides the model for that run. Running claude or codex directly still uses your official login. Nomi must be running. Terminal launch commands are not yet available for Kimi Code or MiniMax Code. Nomi asks for confirmation before updating PATH , adding only a marked block to your shell config (or updating user PATH on Windows) and removing it when you turn the toggle off. # Usage and Model Quality In Settings → Usage analytics : Usage cost : Token usage and cost parsed from local coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, dsh, Grok, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot CLI, Kimi, Aider), alongside official account subscription quotas. Budget, privacy, pricing, and model-data sync settings live here too. See Privacy Security for how logs are read. Comparison / Trends / Requests : Continuously records per-request success rate, time to first token, duration, output speed, and cache hit rate for comparison by model, provider, key, and client. Reported across two scopes: Gateway layer (HTTP requests through the Nomi gateway) and CLI layer (each turn of an agent running in Nomi, including CLI and tool overhead). Only metadata is stored—no chat content—and retained for 30 days by default (configurable to 7 / 30 / 90 days). # Security API keys are encrypted using the OS secure storage (macOS Keychain / Windows DPAPI / Linux Secret Service) and stored locally; the UI only receives masked values. Keys are sent only with requests to the URL you configured for that provider. The gateway listens on localhost only, with each client authenticating via its own token; outbound requests pin the resolved IP to prevent DNS rebinding. Tool-result destinations are evaluated against the actual upstream: cloud providers accessed through the gateway are treated as cloud services, so Only local models can read files and cloud consent prompts apply as usual. Before sending to a third-party provider, secrets in chats, file contents, and command output are replaced with placeholders by default; see Privacy Security . # Environment Variables Providers supplied via DEEPSEEK_API_KEY , OPENAI_API_KEY , ANTHROPIC_API_KEY , GEMINI_API_KEY , or OLLAMA_BASE_URL are loaded read-only and used by default when no model is assigned for Nomi chat. NOMI_PROVIDER= id forces Nomi chat to use a specific provider (locking the model picker and tray menu). # Implementation Gateway: Unified Gateway , implemented in apps/desktop-go/internal/gateway (retry and fallback in server/retry.go ). Provider storage: apps/desktop-go/internal/core/gwstore ( userData/gateway/ ); web links: internal/core/providerlink ; terminal launch commands: internal/core/terminal ; usage: internal/core/usage .
