UI: packages/ai-chat/src/components/ModelsPage , ProviderLink , UsagePanel , and QualityPanel .

d: One-click small models, Ollama, offline mode
x: Entry point: Settings → Models Agents → Local Models , or press Ctrl/⌘+Shift+J to jump straight there. Once a model is downloaded, it works completely offline. # One-Click Open-Source Small Models Built-in model catalog: Qwen3 0.6B / 1.7B / 4B, Qwen2.5 1.5B Instruct, SmolLM2 1.7B Instruct, and Phi-4 mini Instruct—all under permissive open-source licenses (Apache-2.0 / MIT). Recommends suitable models based on your computer's RAM, with each card indicating whether memory is sufficient. Displays the license before download, supports progress tracking and cancellation, and verifies SHA-256 after download. Ollama is not required: downloading a model for the first time automatically fetches the llama.cpp inference runtime. After clicking Start , the model is automatically registered as a local provider; you can click Use for chat , stop it, delete it, or check Run when the app starts . # Ollama (Optional) If Ollama is installed, you can list, pull (with progress), and delete its models here, independent of the built-in engine. Default address: http://127.0.0.1:11434 . Only pull models whose licenses permit your intended use. When using an Ollama model with an agent, start Ollama with a sufficiently large context window: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=20480 ollama serve . The default context length is too small, causing long prompts to be truncated and leading to empty or off-target replies. # Offline Mode Enabling offline mode is equivalent to turning on Only local models can read files (see Privacy Security ): file contents, images, and knowledge base snippets are sent only to local models. If a built-in model is running, it is set as the chat model. # Implementation Inference runs via llama.cpp 's llama-server (MIT), listening only on a random port on 127.0.0.1 and exposing an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Model catalog: apps/desktop-go/internal/core/local/llmcatalog.go (each entry pins its file and SHA-256); service: internal/core/local/service.go ; UI: packages/ai-chat/src/components/LocalPanel .

d: MCP servers, SKILL.md packs, importing from other tools
x: Entry point: Settings → Extensions / MCP , or press Ctrl/⌘+Shift+E to open the extensions panel. It has two tabs: MCP Servers and Skills . # MCP Servers Add local command ( stdio ) or remote HTTP / SSE servers in the UI. Built-in presets include three official reference servers ( filesystem , memory , sequential-thinking ), plus Playwright (official Microsoft preset, operating on the page's accessibility tree without needing a vision model) and Chrome DevTools (official Chrome preset, debugging and controlling Chrome) for web automation. Presets are fetched via npx on first connection rather than bundled with the app, so Node.js must be installed locally. Import JSON accepts standard { mcpServers : { … } } configs to import multiple servers at once. Imported servers start disconnected so you can review them before enabling. Once connected, every tool is listed and tagged as read-only or destructive. Remote server authorization : HTTP / SSE servers requiring sign-in show Authorization required . Clicking Authorize connect completes OAuth login in your browser (with automatic authorization server discovery and PKCE; if a server does not support dynamic client registration, you can enter a Client ID in the server settings). Tokens renew automatically and can be canceled or cleared with Clear authorization at any time. Servers with a manually configured Authorization header bypass browser OAuth. Changing a server's URL, headers, or Client ID clears existing authorization and requires re-authorizing. Trust levels (configured per server): Ask every time (default), Auto-approve read-only (ask for others), or Auto-approve all (still logged). Destructive tools always require explicit confirmation in their details. Every call is written to the local audit log, viewable under Settings → Nomi → Desktop permissions → Activity log . # Skills (SKILL.md) Each folder represents a skill: SKILL.md starts with a name and description, followed by instructions for the assistant, and can include reference files. Only the name and description of enabled skills are injected into chat; the model reads the full file only when needed, saving context. Skills do not execute scripts. Enabled skills can also be invoked directly in Nomi chat with / skill-name . You can create, edit, enable / disable, delete, or import skills from a folder. Two sample skills are included: weekly-report and meeting-notes . # Importing from Other Tools Import from other tools reads local configs from Claude Code ( ~/.claude.json , .mcp.json , ~/.claude/skills ) and Codex ( ~/.codex/config.toml , ~/.agents/skills ), listing MCP servers and skills available to select and import. Imported MCP servers stay disconnected by default; skills are copied into Nomi's skills directory without modifying the original files. # Implementation Core: apps/desktop-go/internal/core/extensions ( mcpconfig.go , service.go , migrate.go , with OAuth in oauth*.go ). OAuth credentials are encrypted per server under userData/extensions/oauth/ ; if OS secure storage is unavailable, authorization is refused rather than falling back to plaintext. Authorization endpoints accept public HTTPS only (except when the server itself is on 127.0.0.1 ), require every resolved IP to be non-private, and do not follow redirects. Tokens are sent only to the configured server URL; the browser callback listens only on 127.0.0.1 , validates state and iss , accepts a single request, and times out after 180 seconds. Configuration is stored in userData/extensions/mcp.json ; environment variables and headers whose names contain key , token , secret , password , auth , cookie , or credential are encrypted via OS secure storage and masked in the UI—saving is refused if OS secure storage is unavailable. Destructive classification does not blindly trust server self-reports: non-read-only tools on local command servers are always treated as destructive, and remote tools are inferred from hazardous names ( exec , delete , write , shell , etc.). Servers can also be supplied via the MCP_SERVERS environment variable (JSON array); they are displayed read-only in the UI and always use Ask every time . Skills are stored under userData/skills/ name /SKILL.md ; reading reference files is restricted to plaintext, capped at 64 KB, and cannot escape the skill directory. UI: packages/ai-chat/src/components/ExtensionsPanel .

d: Files, commands, reminders, clipboard, code sandbox, tool permissions
x: Within the boundaries you grant, Nomi can take actions on your behalf: reading and writing files, setting reminders, reading and writing the clipboard, running commands in a workspace, and executing short code snippets. Every step checks permissions, writes to the audit log, and supports undo for file edits. Settings entry point: Settings → Nomi → Desktop permissions , or via the tray menu Desktop capabilities (file grants / activity log)… . # Files Granted folders : Grant access through the system picker (read-only or read-write), or grant a single file. Nothing is accessible by default. Ask directly: Summarize ~/Documents/report.pdf or Find files mentioning invoice . Nomi can list, search, read, summarize, edit, copy, and move txt , md , pdf , docx , and other files. Nomi chat workspace : Above the input box of a new chat, you can pick a workspace for each Nomi chat (new chats default to Documents/nomi ). Files inside the workspace do not require separate grants; see Privacy Security . Asking Nomi to access a new folder : When Nomi needs a folder outside the workspace, a Folder access request card appears in the chat showing the path and read/write scope: click Grant to allow immediately, or Choose another folder… to open the system picker. Paths that do not exist, are not folders, or are too broad (home directory, system directories, sensitive directories, etc.) must be picked manually. Confirmation : When approval is needed while the chat window is open, an authorization card appears above the input bar (Allow / Reject / Don't ask again for this type of action in this chat / View tool, arguments, and dry-run preview); if the chat window is closed, Nomi shows a speech bubble. Destructive actions and the first send to the cloud expand details immediately, require a 1-second delay before confirmation (to prevent misclicks), and default to reject after 120 seconds without a response. Undo : Deletions only move files to the app trash (kept for 30 days). Under Desktop permissions → Undoable actions , you can undo file changes made by Nomi step by step. Always denied : .ssh , .gnupg , cloud credential directories, keychains, browser profiles, .env , private key files (such as id_rsa , *.kdbx ), and the app's own data directory are never accessible, even if inside a granted folder. Protected folders : Under Desktop permissions → Privacy , you can add your own protected folders (such as finance or identity documents). Just like the built-in blocklist, they remain off-limits even inside a granted folder; agents cannot work in them either and cannot read or write them inside the OS sandbox. Removing protection requires confirmation first. # Commands Nomi can run commands inside the chat workspace ( workspace_run ). Commands run under your user account and are not restricted to the workspace ; whether confirmation is required depends on Auto-review commands and Command allowlist , see Privacy Security . Clicking Always run in this chat on the confirmation card skips further prompts for the same command (in the same working directory) within that chat, and resets in a new chat or after restarting the app; commands that read credentials or publish are never offered this option, and it does not apply in Ask each time mode. # Reminders and Clipboard Reminders : See Scheduling and Tasks . Clipboard : Nomi can read or write the current clipboard ( clipboard_read / clipboard_write ), asking for confirmation the first time it is used in each app run by default. # Controlled Browser (Currently Unavailable) Controlled browser tools (opening pages, reading pages, etc.) still appear in the tool list and Tool permissions , but this version has no browser integration wired up—calling them returns No controlled browser available in the current environment . To let Nomi read or interact with web pages, add the Playwright or Chrome DevTools preset under Extensions / MCP (see MCP and Skills ). # Computer Use Nomi can operate local desktop apps on your behalf (Finder, Notes, System Settings, etc.): it first reads the app's accessibility tree (each button and text field gets a ref ID), then clicks, types, presses shortcuts, and scrolls by ref ID. By default, it does not move the real mouse cursor or steal focus. Setup : Click Install under Settings → Computer Use ; Nomi installs agent-desktop via npm (open source, Apache-2.0; requires Node.js 18 or newer). If the global npm directory is not writable, it can install into a user directory instead. You can Check for updates and update on the same page; only tested major versions are installed (currently 1.x ), and newer major versions only trigger a notification rather than auto-installing. On macOS, grant Accessibility permission under System Settings → Privacy Security → Accessibility to the app that launches agent-desktop , plus Screen Recording for screenshots: macOS attributes both permissions to the host app—Nomi itself when called from Nomi (or the terminal running pnpm dev during development), so granting permission to agent-desktop alone is not enough. The settings page states which app to authorize, shows permission status, and opens the system guide; click Re-check after granting without restarting. These tools are not exposed to models until installed. Pre-installed binaries ( brew install agent-desktop , etc.) are also detected, or you can specify the executable via NOMI_AGENT_DESKTOP . Agents : Once agent-desktop is installed ( Settings → Computer Use → Allow agents to use it , enabled by default), newly launched ACP agent sessions such as Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini receive the nomi-computer MCP server and can use the same tools to operate apps (e.g., opening the app to verify UI changes after editing code). Confirmation cards identify which agent made the request, sharing the same confirmation, auditing, and blocked-app rules as chat; Don't ask again in this chat is tracked per agent tab. While an agent's desktop action waits for your confirmation, the Agent Board marks that tab as waiting for your action. Agents in plan mode can only read the UI (evaluated in real time from the tab's current permission mode, taking effect immediately if switched mid-session). Enabled by default (injected only when agent-desktop is installed); turn it off in Settings → Computer Use to take effect for new sessions. Confirmation : You are prompted on the first UI read and the first action. Clicking Allow permits this action and automatically runs subsequent desktop actions in the same chat (each agent tab counts as one chat), including payments, sending, deleting, submitting, System Settings changes, unlabeled icon-only buttons, shortcuts likely to send or quit/close windows ( Return , ⌘↩ , ⌘Q , ⌘W , Ctrl+Q , Ctrl+W , etc.), and coordinate clicks that move the real cursor. Clicking Always allow (or turning on Run desktop actions automatically under Settings → Computer Use ) applies this across all future chats without step-by-step confirmation after reading a UI, and can be turned off anytime. Before Allow is clicked, those sensitive actions still prompt on first use. Actions targeting password managers, banking apps, or Nomi's own windows (including coordinates landing on those windows) are always rejected and cannot be overridden; emergency stop and audit logging remain active. When Ask each time is selected in the input bar, every action still asks individually. Post-action re-read : After clicking, typing, pressing a key, or scrolling, Nomi automatically re-reads a short slice of the same app's UI by default so the model can confirm the result and get updated ref IDs; the model can disable this when not needed. Vision fallback : For canvases, games, remote desktops, or custom-drawn UIs where elements cannot be read, select a vision-capable model under Settings → Computer Use . Nomi takes a screenshot, sends it to the vision model to locate the target, gets screen coordinates, and clicks by coordinates (which moves the real mouse cursor). Every screenshot prompts for confirmation before sending; when Only local models can read files is on, only local vision models are allowed. Dedicated UI-grounding models such as Alibaba Cloud Bailian GUI-Plus perform better here. Emergency stop : While a desktop action is running, a Using desktop · Stop bar appears at the bottom of the chat window (above the chat column); when the target app is in the foreground, press the global shortcut (default ⌘⇧. / Ctrl+Shift+. , customizable or disableable in Settings → Computer Use ). The stop bar button, settings button, and shortcut all trigger the same path: canceling the active desktop action (regardless of how long it has been running), dismissing any pending desktop-action confirmation cards, and aborting the active turn (whether Nomi chat or an agent tab, including turns waiting on a confirmation card). All further desktop actions in that turn are rejected until you send the next message. The Dynamic Island does not display operating desktop status. Isolated mode (macOS, Apple Silicon; requires an agent-desktop version with the sandbox command—not yet in 1.2.0 , and hidden from Settings when unavailable): Selecting an agent-desktop sandbox in Settings runs all desktop actions inside that isolated macOS VM without touching your host desktop. Create the sandbox in a terminal first ( agent-desktop sandbox install macos , then agent-desktop sandbox create name --provider macos --set ipsw=latest ), then enable Remote Login and grant Accessibility inside the VM on first boot; Settings lets you start and stop the sandbox. Blocked apps : Password managers, keychains, banking and payment apps, and Nomi's own windows are blocked. You can add more under Settings → Computer Use → Blocked apps (additions only—built-in blocks cannot be relaxed; app names match by case-insensitive substring, and bundle IDs match by full segment or prefix such as com.tencent. ). When a model targets an app by name, Nomi locates the running app and checks both name and bundle ID; if identity cannot be resolved or the app behind a name changes after reading the UI, the action is rejected. Full-screen captures (screenshots and vision fallback without a target app) are blocked whenever a blocked app has a visible window or when the window list cannot be retrieved, requiring an explicit target app instead. Privacy : UI contents are sent only to the current turn's model for that turn (cloud models cannot read them when Only local models can read files is enabled). You can turn on Hide text-field contents when reading the UI in Settings so text fields expose only character counts. Screenshots are saved locally under userData/desktop/screenshots/ and sent to a vision model only during vision fallback (with your confirmation). Typed text is never passed as command-line arguments (including in isolated mode: if the sandbox command cannot forward stdin , typing fails rather than falling back to CLI arguments), and the audit log records only hashes and lengths; agent-initiated actions are tagged as cli: agent-name in the activity log. Limitations : Available only in foreground chats (background tasks cannot operate the desktop). Linux Wayland sessions support reading the UI and acting by ref ID only, not screenshots or coordinate clicks. Electron apps, games, and custom-drawn UIs may not expose accessible elements. # Code Sandbox Nomi can run short JavaScript or Python snippets, always showing the code in a dialog for your confirmation first. Code can read and write only its per-run temporary directory, is terminated automatically on timeout (15s default, 60s max), deletes the temporary directory afterward, and receives no API keys in its environment. # Tool Permissions Under Desktop permissions → Tool permissions , each read/write tool can be set to Always allow , Ask once per run , or Ask every time . Destructive tools and code execution are fixed to Ask every time . The permission mode in Nomi chat's input bar (Plan / Ask each time / Auto-edit files / Auto) also governs prompt frequency; see Privacy Security . # Activity Log Every desktop tool invocation logs its timestamp, outcome, and arguments (storing only argument hashes and lengths), retained for the last 30 days and viewable paginated under Desktop permissions → Activity log . Clear all desktop capability data removes all folder grants, tool permission settings, and activity records. # Implementation Core: apps/desktop-go/internal/core/desktop (grants and path checks in path_guard.go , confirmation in permission_broker.go / consent.go , audit in audit_log.go , undo in undo_journal.go , trash in app_trash.go , command review in command_review.go ), with tool definitions in internal/ai/runtime/igtools . File parsing runs inside a restricted subprocess ( internal/core/desktop/parse ). Reading files in the workspace or granted folders does not count as external content; once a turn reads external content such as web pages, command output, or MCP responses, write actions in the same turn ask for confirmation again to prevent prompt-injected edits (you can click Always allow to skip further prompts in that chat). Code sandbox: apps/desktop-go/internal/core/sandbox . JavaScript uses the local Node permission model ( node --permission , restricted to the temporary directory); Python prefers OS sandboxing (macOS sandbox-exec / Linux bwrap ) and falls back to python3 -I when unavailable or on Windows, noting the mode in the result; see Security Boundaries . Computer Use: Executor in apps/desktop-go/internal/core/computer (invoking agent-desktop CLI, parsing JSON output, ref caching, single re-lookup by role and name after UI changes, app blocklist and sensitive-action checks in guard.go , install and update checks in install.go , settings in settings.go , activity tracking and emergency stop in activity.go , vision grounding in vision.go , isolated sandbox in sandbox.go , computer.* contract handlers in register.go ), vision model calls via gateway in internal/core/gwstore/vision.go , emergency-stop wiring (aborting chats, dismissing confirmation cards, locking agent tabs until the next turn) in apps/desktop-go/computer_wiring.go , global shortcuts via shell.GlobalShortcuts (Wails GlobalShortcutManager ), tools in internal/ai/runtime/igtools/deskcomputer.go , settings UI in packages/ai-chat/src/components/SettingsView/ComputerSection.tsx and ComputerOptions.tsx , and the chat stop bar in packages/ai-chat/src/components/ComputerActivityBar . MCP for agents: internal/core/computer/mcpserve . The core opens a POST-only endpoint on 127.0.0.1 (validating Host and rejecting browser requests with an Origin header). Each agent tab gets a random token written to a 0600 file under userData/harness/computer-mcp/ (cleared on startup, invalidated when the tab closes; the OS sandbox grants read access only to that tab's own file so other tabs cannot read it). Agents launch Nomi executable --computer-mcp token-file as a stdio MCP server, which starts no UI and forwards stdio to the endpoint; tokens never appear in CLI arguments or agent configs. Injection is handled in internal/core/cli/harness/computer_mcp.go (Claude Code via --mcp-config with tools pre-allowed while confirmation stays in Nomi; Codex via -c mcp_servers.nomi-computer.* ; ACP session/new mcpServers ), with OS sandbox read access allowed specifically for the token directory. Data is stored under userData/desktop/ (settings, audit logs, activity records, trash, and screenshots).

d: Unified workspace, direct CLI bases, images and files, image generation, command palette
x: Open the chat window from the tray menu ( Open AI Chat ), the desktop character (when enabled), or Ctrl/⌘+N . # Unified Workspace and Conversation Base Nomi 2.5 unifies chat and coding sessions in a single sidebar: Direct CLI base in main chat : Select Nomi or any locally installed official CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, etc.) per conversation right inside the main chat, and switch back to resume that CLI's native session seamlessly. Agent tabs and endpoint filtering : Pick an agent from the sidebar's New conversation menu (or press Ctrl/⌘+T ) to open a dedicated agent tab; the left navigation rail lists each endpoint vertically so one click filters sessions by endpoint. See agents . On-demand side workspace : Open the multi-tab side workspace from the title bar whenever you need side-by-side diff review, project files, split terminal, run traces, native browser, or side chat. When creating a new Nomi chat, if an empty conversation with no messages already exists in the current workspace, Nomi switches to it instead of creating another empty one. You choose an initial endpoint from the New conversation menu at creation time, and main-chat conversations can switch bases directly via the model/base selector. # Chat Streaming responses. On the left is the conversation list (grouped by project; see personalization ), which can be collapsed or expanded with Ctrl/⌘+B or the button next to the title bar; when collapsed, hovering over Chat in the navigation rail opens the session panel as a floating overlay. Above the input bar of a new session is Project · Branch , where you can search, switch, create, or clear a project (multi-folder projects display as Name +N , with hover showing all folders; the branch reflects the primary folder). Once you send the first message, the project is locked in and no longer shown in the top bar. Use Ctrl/⌘+Shift+F to search conversations. Enter sends; Alt/Option+Enter or Shift+Enter inserts a newline. Press ↑ in an empty input box to recall your previous prompt, or type / to open slash commands . Single-line input bar (Codex-style, with borderless buttons): the + menu and permission mode sit on the left, while the model selector, voice controls, and send button sit on the right. The + menu attaches items to the current message: images or files (same as drag-and-drop or paste), file or folder references (inserts @ when a workspace is selected), handoff to an agent (in Nomi chats, lists installed agents and shows Hand off to X above the input bar, same as /agent ), and the knowledge base Q A toggle; agent tabs also include Plugins / Commands . Switch models from the model button; settings live at the bottom of the left navigation rail. Each reply shows the model used beneath it. If you switch models mid-conversation, a note appears at the end indicating that the new model will continue with the prior context. Transcript view : The global default is under Settings → General → Appearance → Transcript view (initially Thinking ). New sessions and sessions without a per-session override use this default. The menu in the title bar lets you pick a separate level for the current session, overriding the global default; each session remembers its setting across restarts (agent tabs remember by session, so closing a tab and reopening the same session from history keeps the setting; forked sessions inherit the global default). Use global default at the bottom of the menu clears the per-session override. Applies to both Nomi chats and agent tabs: Normal : Tool calls between two replies fold into one summary line per kind (Explore / Command / Edit / Other; items of the same kind do not have to be adjacent, at most one line per kind per segment, ordered by first appearance), e.g., Explored 3 files, 2 searches , Ran 2 commands , Edited 1 file +12 −3 . An active category shows the step currently running (e.g., Running command pnpm test ), and failure counts appear on the corresponding line. Click to expand individual steps, and click a step to view arguments and output. Thinking is not shown separately (if a segment only has thinking, a single Thought line is shown). Subtask cards, mid-turn injected messages, and generated images still appear individually. Thinking : Tool calls still fold into one line per kind; thinking blocks between two replies are combined into a separate block (expanded while running, collapsed when done, with duration counting only thinking time). Verbose : Every tool call appears on its own line without folding; arguments, output, thinking content, and subagents are expanded by default. When collapsed, the thinking line displays Thought for N seconds plus the first sentence of the thinking block; while running, it displays Thinking and the sentence currently in progress. Active thinking and tool steps show a flowing gray gradient shimmer across the text (static when the system Reduce motion setting is enabled). When the knowledge base or long-term memory is used, replies show citations and how many memories were referenced. When a conversation nears capacity (~95%), earlier messages are automatically compacted into a summary before sending, or you can run /compact manually with an optional focus (e.g., /compact focus on the API design ). Capacity is judged from actual context usage in the previous turn rather than estimation alone. The summary is organized into sections ( Requirements, Decisions, Files Code, Errors Fixes, Results, To-dos, Current Work ), followed by recently read or edited files, the latest plan, and used skills; long-term memories already supplied to the model before compaction are preserved alongside it. When actual usage in the previous turn exceeds ~60%, large outputs in tool records older than the last 3 turns are trimmed to keep only their beginning and end, allowing raw conversation text to stay intact longer before compaction is needed. The trimmed boundary only advances when usage exceeds the threshold again, keeping the prefix sent on each turn unchanged so prompt caching is not broken. During multi-step tool loops in a turn (reading files, running commands), each step checks actual usage: when approaching capacity, earlier large tool outputs keep only their beginning and end, and Nomi re-reads them if needed; if still near capacity, earlier steps in the current turn are compacted into a summary before continuing; if the model still reports a context-length error, Nomi compacts further and retries that step once instead of failing immediately. Background Nomi tasks follow the same behavior. Command and code outputs exceeding the cap (30,000 characters for commands) preserve the beginning and end while eliding the middle, ensuring errors and failing test cases are not truncated away. When any tool output exceeds 30,000 characters, Nomi first inspects the head and tail and reads the middle in pages if needed (kept only for the active run and inaccessible from other chats; read content remains subject to Only local models can read files ). Saying done does not mean the turn is done: if the current turn's plan ( plan_update ) still has unfinished steps, Nomi is prompted to continue or mark unachievable steps as skipped with a reason, up to two reminders per turn; if nothing is done after a reminder, prompting stops. During automatic continuation, if a turn only edits the plan or repeats identical calls, it stops instead of spinning. Thinking content from previous turns is not re-sent with history (protocols other than Anthropic count it toward input tokens). On-demand tools stay enabled for the rest of the conversation once activated, and the system prompt does not vary by topic, preserving prefix caching. Execution traces and /context display the cache hit rate from the previous turn. Like Codex, tool calls and results from previous turns (read files, command outputs) are passed into the next turn verbatim rather than as reply text alone; previously sent content is re-sent verbatim each turn to work with provider prompt caching (Anthropic cache breakpoints, OpenAI prompt_cache_key ), so follow-up turns mostly hit cache. From a conversation row's menu, you can rename, delete, or Fork… ; each reply also has a Fork from here action that keeps history only up to that reply. Ctrl/⌘+Shift+F directly forks the current conversation into a new one. # Where Conversations Are Stored Conversations (entries for Nomi chats and agent tabs in the sidebar) are stored by the core in userData/conversations/ : File Contents index.json Conversation list (name, endpoint, workspace, updated time, etc.), message counts, active ID previews.json First 300 characters of each conversation's first user message (for sidebar search) migrated.json Marker indicating legacy localStorage data has been imported (also recorded in index.json ) messages/ id .jsonl One message per line New messages are appended to the end of the .jsonl file; edit-and-resend, clear, fork, and exceeding the maximum retained message count rewrite the whole file. Full rewrites and index updates write to a temporary file first and then rename atomically with 0600 file permissions. The chat window keeps messages in memory only for the dozen or so most recently opened conversations (plus the active conversation and any not yet persisted to the core); others are loaded from the core when opened. Writes: the UI updates first, and writes are queued sequentially to the core (one at a time; as soon as one returns, the next is sent without batching). If a write fails temporarily (disconnected socket, disk error), it backs off and retries a few times; if it still fails, it stays in the queue without data loss and retries after ~15 seconds or on the next write, showing a one-time Conversation history could not be saved right now notice. If the core reports the conversation missing (failed to create or index rebuilt), it recreates the conversation from the UI's title and full message list and continues writing; retried appends perform a full rewrite to avoid duplicates. Writes rejected by the core for invalid arguments are not retried and show the same notice. On exit (tray, ⌘Q , log out), the core waits for queued chat window writes to finish before closing: up to 1.5 seconds, exiting immediately once 200 ms have passed with no pending writes. The remaining risk window is a message generated in the last few milliseconds before exit that has not yet reached the core, or a write still waiting in retry. If index.json is corrupted (invalid JSON), it is moved to index.json.corrupt (with a timestamp added if one already exists, never overwriting), and the conversation list is rebuilt from messages/*.jsonl (name taken from the first user message, timestamp from the message, marked recovered ; empty conversations are not recovered and the active conversation pointer is lost). The same rebuild runs if index.json is missing while message files exist. Migration status relies on migrated.json , so a rebuild will not re-import from legacy localStorage . If index.json cannot be read (permissions or I/O error), it is not treated as empty: all reads and writes fail, and the chat window shows Conversation history is temporarily unreadable with a Retry button instead of showing an empty list or triggering migration. On startup, a boot screen prevents a blank window: it fetches the conversation list (5-second timeout per attempt, up to 3 retries) and shows progress during the initial legacy conversation import. In 2.2.0 and earlier, conversations lived in the chat window's localStorage (~5 MB WebKit quota, which failed when full). On first launch of 2.3.0, those conversations (plus old chats extracted from the 2.0.4 Electron version) are imported into the core in parallel, verified by count, and marked complete; unfinished imports resume on the next launch without overwriting existing conversations. Conversation IDs follow the same rule as the core (letters, digits, _ , - , excluding Windows reserved names such as con , nul , com1 , validated by isValidConversationId in the contract); invalid legacy IDs are mapped to deterministic new IDs ( m_ hash _ usable_suffix ) with the original ID recorded in metadata legacyId . Legacy localStorage keys are kept for one release so downgrading back to 2.2.0 still shows conversations from that point (newer messages are not included). Export data in Settings packages all of userData/conversations/ into conversations/ inside a zip archive ( conversations.json contains only chat preferences). There is no in-app restore from export archives; exports are for inspection or personal backup. # Images and Files Paste or drag and drop images into the input box: up to 4 per message, max 20 MB each (PNG / JPEG / WebP / GIF / BMP), automatically compressed before sending. Conversation history saves only thumbnails; originals are not written to disk. Requires a vision-capable model; local vision models (such as Ollama's qwen2.5vl or llava ) work too. When Only local models can read files is enabled, images are not sent to cloud models; cloud models ask for your consent before receiving an image for the first time. Up to 10 other files can be attached: text files up to 200 KB are sent with their contents, while larger or binary files pass only their local path for the model to read with tools. # Image Generation and Asset Library Assign an image generation model to Nomi under Settings → Models Agents → Task Cost Routing (defaults to Auto , picking the image model from the same provider as the chat model), then ask Nomi to generate images directly. Generated images and images produced by agents go into the sidebar's Asset Library : Filter by category (Illustration / Character / Landscape / Animal / Other), source, and search (prompt, filename, tags). The top-right corner shows used storage (actual size of all images). Auto-categorized after generation: first matched by prompt keywords, then classified by the auxiliary model (the same model used for command review; falls back to keywords only if unconfigured or if the model is in the cloud without your consent). Older images are categorized by keywords. In the masonry grid, metadata stays on the card: category in the top-left, source and resolution along the bottom; click to inspect the prompt in the detail view. Click an image to open the detail view: full-screen preview, actual resolution in the top-left, copy image, and under More : download, reveal in folder, or delete (moves to system trash). Navigate left/right or via the bottom thumbnail strip. The right pane shows filename, prompt, editable tags, editable category, asset info, and related images in the same category; you can also edit from this image, use it as a reference image, or regenerate (which calls the image model again). The Asset Library does not include uploads: it only stores generated images. Original images you send in chat are stored in the local chat directory ( userData/chat/images/user-… ) and can be viewed, downloaded, or used with Edit / Use as reference from the message bubble, without appearing in the Asset Library list. Transient image service failures (network, timeout, rate limit, server error) automatically retry twice; if the image was already generated and only downloading failed, only the download is retried without regenerating. Auth and parameter errors are not retried. # Command Palette Press Ctrl/⌘+K to search all actions (new chat, feature panels, voice toggles, etc.) and every Settings section. # Handing Off to Agents (Delegation) Nomi can hand off specific coding, documentation, review, and research tasks to local agents. Tasks run in the background by default : once dispatched, you can keep chatting with Nomi, and results return to the conversation when finished. Ask naturally, e.g., Have Codex fix the login bug , or use /agent codex fix the login bug to specify the agent. The command dispatches immediately, passing along any attached images' Asset Library paths; requests over 4,000 characters are not dispatched and prompt you to shorten them first. You can click Stop while waiting for confirmation. If dispatch fails (not installed, delegation disabled, no workspace selected, user declined, or stopped), the chat states the reason directly instead of letting the chat model reply as if the handoff succeeded. Typing /agent codex alone queues it for your next message (shown above the input bar; click to cancel). Before dispatching, confirmation follows Nomi's permission mode ( Plan mode never dispatches). When a workspace is selected for the conversation, the agent starts in that workspace (or a subdirectory inside it). Delegated agents run at the highest permission level the target agent supports ( Full access for agents that support it, or Ask each time for others such as MiniMax), independent of Nomi's current mode or the Auto-approve everything toggle; the pre-approval confirmation card explicitly displays the effective permission level and applicable host protections. Each subtask opens as a background agent tab using that agent's default source for new tabs (official account or third-party provider). The subtask card in chat shows progress, subagents, and pending approvals, and can be stopped individually. When finished, the result appears in the conversation along with modified files and generated images (same for image generation tasks delegated to background Nomi), which Nomi can read on the next turn. Background Nomi writes results in the language you used to assign the task (English prompts produce English results). Click View on a subtask card to open the subtask in a side panel next to the chat while the main conversation stays in place and both update live. The side panel uses the same message list, input bar, prompt cards, and queued-message controls as the main chat (model, permissions, attachments, and slash commands belong to the subtask's own tab rather than competing with the main thread). Sending while running injects a message (if unsupported, waits until the current turn finishes), Stop interrupts the turn, and sending while idle starts another turn. Results from subsequent turns also flow back into the main chat. Press Esc or click Close to leave the side panel without switching away from the main thread. Subagents inside an agent ( Task / spawn_agent ) and tasks delegated to background Nomi can also open in the same side panel: if steps are available, they render with the same message view; if there is no separate follow-up channel, the reason is shown, and stoppable tasks can be stopped. See Subagent Chat Parity for the design. The Session details button to the left of the file panel toggle in the title bar (visible once messages exist) opens a column on the right side of the chat card (without covering messages; the chat area narrows accordingly with padding around it; click again or press Esc to collapse, and its toggle state is remembered). Both lists show 5 items initially with … to expand the rest; empty sections are hidden. Opening the middle diff or file preview pane automatically collapses this column regardless of window width; when the window width is under 1440 px, opening the file panel or subtask side panel also collapses it to leave room for the chat; on wider screens, it stays open when the file panel or subtask side panel opens, switching to an overlay anchored at the top-right of the chat column without squeezing messages (clicking outside does not dismiss it; click the button again or press Esc to close). After an auto-collapse, clicking the button reopens it as an overlay at the top-right of the chat column (even with the middle pane open, it sits over the chat rather than covering the diff or file preview) without squeezing the chat; clicking outside the overlay or pressing Esc dismisses it, and changing those pane toggles restores the automatic rules. Approvals on delegated tabs wait up to 10 minutes (2 minutes on tabs you open yourself). When finished, the agent reports in a fixed structure: what was done, which files were changed, what remains unfinished, and what needs your decision. Settings: Settings → Nomi → Permissions Handoff contains the master toggle and default assignments by task type (Coding, Specs Docs, Code Review, Research); choosing Let Nomi choose picks from installed agents. No agent installed, or delegation disabled : Nomi stops proposing handoffs and handles the work directly using file tools to read code, fs_edit for incremental edits, and workspace_run to build and run tests (requires selecting a workspace for the conversation). # Long-Running Tasks For multi-step work, Nomi first outlines a checklist via plan_update (steps with In Progress / Done) and updates it as each step finishes so progress stays visible in chat. A single turn allows up to 20 consecutive tool calls; if Nomi still needs more tool calls when the limit is reached, it continues automatically for another turn without you typing continue , up to 20 automatic continuations regardless of token usage. Auto-continuation stops if you rejected a step during that turn. When stopped, the end of the reply explains why, and saying continue resumes from there. You can click Stop at any time. On continuation turns, large tool outputs from earlier in the turn (read files, test logs) keep only their opening section to avoid filling context; Nomi re-reads them if needed. Tools are supplied on demand so unused ones do not occupy context: file-viewing tools are always present when a workspace is selected; file-writing tools (create, modify, move, delete) appear when the conversation discusses making changes; delegation tools for agents or background Nomi appear when discussing coding tasks, extended work (documents, reports, image sets, background jobs), or progress checks, along with the rules for doing it directly vs. handing off. Once provided, they stay available to preserve prompt caching. File reads default to 4,000 characters per call and searches default to 20 results; Nomi reads further or increases the limit when needed. When uncertain, Nomi asks you above the input bar ( ask_user ): one card at a time, lettered options, custom input on the last row, and optional multi-select. Press Enter to continue (advances to the next question if any) or Esc to skip the card with an optional note below. Answering, skipping, clicking Stop, emergency stop, closing the session, or waiting 10 minutes without a reply resumes or ends the turn; on skip or timeout, Nomi proceeds with the safest approach and states its assumptions. Questions from Claude Code, Codex (app-server questions and form-style MCP elicitation), and ACP ( elicitation/create forms) use the same card. Tool allow/deny prompts for commands, file edits, and ACP still use their dedicated cards. When Codex falls back to exec , there is no interactive channel for questions. # Sidebar The bottom of the sidebar holds app-level entries: Settings, Knowledge · Memory · Schedule ( Ctrl/⌘+Shift+M , right drawer), and Extensions / MCP ( Ctrl/⌘+Shift+E ). When a new version finishes downloading, Restart to update appears on the right side of the title bar (to the left of the Transcript view button), or at the bottom of the Settings navigation while on the Settings page. Above the conversation list are Tasks (see Scheduling and Tasks ) and Asset Library . Main window position and size are remembered. # Implementation UI: packages/ai-chat/src ( App.tsx handles assembly only; state lives in app/ : panel toggles, commands and shortcuts, slash commands, right column; plus components/Sidebar , components/MessageInput , components/AssetLibrary ). Conversation storage: Core in apps/desktop-go/internal/core/convstore (contract conversations.* , handlers in internal/core/shellhandlers/conversations.go ); UI in packages/ai-chat/src/services/conversationStore.ts (sync facade + message cache + ordered write queue), conversationBoot.ts (startup index fetch and migration), conversationMigration.ts (legacy localStorage import), components/BootScreen (boot screen); shutdown write drain in shellhandlers.ConversationWrites ( OnShutdown in main.go ). Images open in a dedicated viewer; HTML, PDF, Office, CSV, audio, and video files open with the system default application, while local file access still passes through the core's path and authorization checks.

d: Answers from your folders, with citations
x: Entry points: Settings → Knowledge Memory → Knowledge Base , or open the same tab in the right drawer via the Knowledge · Memory · Schedule icon at the bottom of the sidebar or Ctrl/⌘+Shift+M . Toggle Knowledge base Q A from the input bar's More features menu or with Ctrl/⌘+Shift+K . # Adding Sources Click Add folder to choose folders via the system picker; adding a folder grants read-only access to it, and you can remove it at any time. Supports txt, Markdown, csv, json, yaml, html, common source code files, PDF (citations include page numbers), docx, odt, rtf, and xlsx. Hidden directories, node_modules , dist , build , and files larger than 30 MB are skipped; sensitive directories (such as .ssh and browser profiles) are never read. Text inside images cannot be indexed yet: the panel includes an OCR toggle ( Recognize text in images (OCR) ) and language data download, but OCR is not implemented in this release—enabling it causes image files to fail indexing (without affecting other files). # Answers with Citations When Knowledge base Q A is enabled, Nomi retrieves relevant passages first and lets the active model answer based on them in the language of your question. Inline [1] , [2] markers in the response are clickable citations: preview the passage, open the file, or reveal it in the folder. Chunks cited per answer controls how many passages are attached to the model—higher values give broader coverage while using more context. The Search test tab lets you enter a query and inspect which passages are retrieved. # Retrieval Quality Uses fully local keyword search (BM25) by default, which works well for Chinese as well and requires no extra setup. Under Vectors reranking , you can connect an embedding model (local Ollama nomic-embed-text or bge-m3 recommended) and a reranking service supporting the /rerank endpoint to improve relevance further. Select services from providers already configured in Settings → Models Agents . Before sending file passages to a cloud embedding or reranking service, Nomi asks for separate consent; when Only local models can read files is enabled, nothing is ever sent to the cloud. # Updating the Index Incremental updates run automatically ~20 seconds after startup and every 30 minutes thereafter. You can also click Update index or Rebuild all at any time. # Implementation Core: apps/desktop-go/internal/core/knowledge (hybrid ranking combining BM25 and optional vectors), file parsing in internal/core/desktop/parse ; data stored in userData/knowledge . d: What Nomi remembers and how to manage it
x: Entry points: Settings → Knowledge Memory → Long-Term Memory , or open the same tab in the right drawer via the Knowledge · Memory · Schedule icon at the bottom of the sidebar or Ctrl/⌘+Shift+M . # What Nomi Remembers Conversation memories : When you close the window, start a new conversation, or every 10 messages, Nomi summarizes the conversation into a Title + Summary + Keywords entry; you can also click Summarize this conversation . Summarization uses the active chat model. About me : Long-term facts you state explicitly (preferred name, preferences, goals, etc.) are extracted automatically during summarization and can be added, edited, or deleted; you can also tell Nomi directly to remember… . Passwords, keys, ID numbers, and other sensitive data are filtered out. User profile : A Markdown file you write yourself (name, work, habits, how you want the assistant to respond), referenced in every conversation; stored in persona.md and editable in any text editor. Reply preference profile : Rule-extracted reply preferences (language / style / tone), which can be reset at any time. # Natural Recall Before each prompt, Nomi retrieves relevant memories as background context and indicates in the reply how many memories were referenced. Recall at most adjusts the maximum count. Enabling vector search in the knowledge base improves recall accuracy. Matching only one or two generic words (such as current or what ) does not count as relevant: recall requires matching at least roughly a quarter of the words in your question, and past conversation summaries carry at most 160 characters each. Memories already brought into a conversation stay in context without being injected repeatedly; when a conversation is compacted, recalled memories are preserved alongside the summary. After editing your user profile, the very next message picks up the updated version. # Management Search (press / to focus), edit, pin (prioritized during recall), or forget individual memories; manually edited entries are never overwritten by automatic summarization. Forgetting truly forgets: deleting a conversation summary also deletes the About me entries extracted from it; future summaries of that conversation only look at messages sent after the deletion, and deleted entries will not be re-extracted. If you manually add the same fact yourself, your manual entry takes precedence. Clearing all memories follows the same rule. Any in-flight summarization running at the time of deletion is discarded so pre-deletion content is never written back. Under Settings Export , you can disable long-term memory or auto-summarization, export memories to JSON or Markdown, or clear all memories (both conversation memories and About me ; cannot be undone). When long-term memory is turned off, new conversations are no longer summarized and memories are not referenced in replies; existing memories remain intact. # Implementation Data is stored locally in userData/memory/ ( memory.json , settings.json , persona.md ) and never uploaded. Recall uses BM25 plus optional vectors (reusing the service configured under Knowledge Base → Vectors reranking , subject to the same cloud consent and Only local models can read files restrictions). AI tools: memory_search and memory_remember ; writes are recorded in the local audit log. Core: apps/desktop-go/internal/core/memory ; UI: packages/ai-chat/src/components/MemoryPanel .

d: Reminders, jobs, proactive chat, do-not-disturb, persistent tasks
x: # Schedule Entry points: Settings → Knowledge Memory → Schedule , or open the same tab in the right drawer via the Knowledge · Memory · Schedule icon at the bottom of the sidebar or Ctrl/⌘+Shift+M . Reminders, scheduled tasks, proactive chat, and do-not-disturb settings all live here. # Reminders One-time or recurring: once, daily, weekdays, specific day of the week, monthly, or every N minutes, plus quick presets like In 5 minutes and Tomorrow at this time . You can also ask in chat directly, e.g., Remind me about standup every weekday at 9 AM . When due, Nomi waves and shows a reminder card in her bubble (OK / Snooze 10 minutes). When Nomi is not on the desktop, alerts use the Dynamic Island or system notifications—see How Alerts Are Delivered below. Reminders missed while the app was closed are delivered on the next launch. # Scheduled Tasks Set a name, prompt, schedule, and recurrence rule; when due, the active chat model generates the output, writes it to the chat window, and notifies you per the delivery rules below. The built-in Daily briefing template combines today's reminders with your long-term memory. Tasks missed within the last 12 hours run once on startup; you can also click Run now . # Proactive Chat (Off by Default) When enabled, Nomi occasionally initiates a chat while you are idle using topics from your long-term memory. Choose between Low (up to once a day), Medium (3 times), or High (6 times), and optionally restrict it to specific hours. She never interrupts right after you chatted, while you are away from the computer, or during do-not-disturb hours. Click Try one now to trigger manually. # Do Not Disturb Configure do-not-disturb hours (can span midnight, e.g., 22:30–08:00 ). Nothing pops up during this window: due reminders are queued and delivered together once it ends, while scheduled tasks still run and write results silently to the chat window. # How Alerts Are Delivered Reminders, scheduled task results, proactive chats, agent updates, and usage budget alerts each appear in only one place: Nomi is on the desktop : Uses her speech bubble only (reminders show as reminder cards). Nomi is closed or hidden : Uses the Dynamic Island ; if the Dynamic Island is off, unsupported on the platform, or disabled for that source, falls back to a system notification (clicking opens the chat window). Do-not-disturb hours : Nothing pops up. # Tasks The Tasks entry above the sidebar conversation list lets you assign something once: Nomi remembers it, advances it on a schedule or event, and reaches out when your input is needed. A badge shows how many items require your attention. Create : Say Every day at 9 AM help me… in chat, or click New task and fill out the form: goal, trigger (once, daily, weekdays, every N minutes, manual, or when something happens ), assignee (Nomi, an agent, or notification only), allowed capabilities, and completion behavior (auto-accept or wait for your review; defaults to auto-accept). Before creation, an authorization card lists the goal, capabilities, authorized folders, and expiration for your confirmation. Event triggers : Watch web pages / RSS feeds, GitHub repositories (issue and PR activity, CI completion), read-only tools on local MCP servers, or in-app events (agent turn completed, knowledge base updated). New event-driven tasks initially only record what they observe; enable automatic handling in the task detail pane when ready. Capability levels : Notification only → Read-only (files, web, local records) → Local write (knowledge base, memory, files in authorized folders) → Run commands (still checked by command review) → External actions (such as commenting on GitHub or opening PRs from a nomi/ branch; authorized per action and never auto-merged). File reads and writes are restricted to authorized folders. Tasks delegated to an agent can also pre-allow specific sandbox categories (such as cloud account credentials) so they run without prompting; tasks with external GitHub actions automatically include SSH and Git credentials needed to push code. See agents . Judge by risk (L3 and up, on by default): Commands first go through command review (the same mechanism used for automatic command review in chat) and run directly if approved. Only high-risk commands, credential or never-auto-allow commands, commands rejected by review, or actions taken after reading external content (event triggers) pause to ask you. Unchecking Judge by risk when creating a task prompts on every command. Where no OS-level agent sandbox is available (Windows / Linux, where sandbox.Supported() is false), regular background tasks still confirm each command unless the parent Nomi is in Auto mode; with an OS sandbox active and Auto-approve everything enabled in the foreground, regular background tasks likewise stop prompting per command (except for credentials, destructive actions, and actions after reading external event content). Background agent tasks delegated from Nomi chat always run at the highest permission level the target agent supports ( Full access for agents that support it, or the highest available level) with risk-based command judgment, regardless of Nomi's own mode, the foreground Auto-approve everything toggle, or OS sandbox availability; the pre-approval confirmation card shows the effective permission level and applicable host protections. Command review sends the full command text to the auxiliary model (with secrets, tokens, and local paths redacted first). Approval requests time out after a limit (10 minutes by default), treating timeouts as rejections and marking the task Interrupted: approval needed rather than hanging indefinitely on Waiting for approval . Agent execution : By default, agents edit directly in the codebase; if parallel tasks in the same repository touch the same file, the higher-priority task edits first. An isolated git worktree is created only when explicitly branching from another ref; on acceptance (when auto-accept is off), small diffs copy back to the workspace while larger diffs commit to a new nomi/… branch for you to merge. Tasks of the same kind reuse the previous session. Agents dispatched by Nomi from chat auto-accept on completion and return results directly to the conversation instead of waiting for manual review. Expiration : Tasks are not cut off by token, duration, or cost limits and run until completion (stalled executions without activity time out); authorizations carry an expiration date and can be renewed before expiring. Review and control : Status has four buckets: Scheduled / Running / Needs you (waiting for approval, input, review, verification, or failed) / Done. Both list and board views filter by status and search by title and goal. The list uses two-column cards (matching the Agent Board layout), while the board groups columns by status or priority; cards let you run scheduled tasks immediately or pause running ones. Click a card to inspect details on the right: approve, provide input, accept or send back, pause, cancel, revoke authorization, and view run history and event logs. External actions that were in flight when the app closed are automatically reconciled on restart, asking you to confirm only if automatic verification fails. When an agent delegated from Nomi chat finishes, results return to the conversation for follow-up (replying sends it back for rework) and are no longer marked Waiting for review on the Agent Board or Dynamic Island; you can still accept or send back from the Tasks page. Existing reminders and scheduled tasks also appear as two read-only groups in the list (clicking opens Schedule). # Apps Accounts Settings → Apps Accounts manages external accounts available to tasks. Currently supports GitHub: use your local gh login directly or paste a token (a read-only fine-grained token suffices for watching specific repositories). Credentials stay where they live ( gh or the OS keychain), and tasks can only access them per their granted authorization; removing a connection pauses tasks that depend on it until reauthorized. # Implementation Reminders: apps/desktop-go/internal/core/desktop/reminders ( userData/desktop/reminders.json ); scheduled tasks, proactive chat, and do-not-disturb: internal/core/schedule ( userData/schedule/ ). Tasks: apps/desktop-go/internal/core/tasks ( userData/tasks/ ), event sources in tasks/event_*.go ; connections: internal/core/connections . Never triggers while speaking, thinking, or playing another action, and is completely disabled when the system Reduce motion setting is on. # Display Mode Shows a static illustration by default. Nomi is the only built-in character; character switching and custom model imports are not supported. More → Credits on the toolbar lists the authors and licenses of the character and icons. See Brand Guidelines for brand rules. # Toolbar Vertical toolbar beside the character: AI Chat, Voice (click to mute, right-click for voice preferences), and other frequent controls; the rest live under More (size, close Nomi, quit app, etc.). Fades out when idle, appears when the cursor approaches, and flips automatically to the opposite side near screen edges. Closing Nomi hides her from the desktop and stops voice playback and wake-word listening; alerts are routed through the Dynamic Island or system notifications instead. You can reopen her under Settings → General → Startup Window . # Size Defaults to 50%, adjustable from 30% to 150% (based on a 420×450 character box at 100%); on smaller screens, the upper bound scales down automatically to fit the work area. Entry point Usage Ctrl / ⌘ + Scroll Hold Ctrl ( ⌘ on macOS) and scroll over the character Context menu Right-click the character → Zoom in / Zoom out Settings → General Nomi size slider and reset under Startup Window The bottom-center anchor under her feet stays pinned on screen while resizing; the size value is saved locally and persists across launches. # Interaction Settings Tray → Interaction settings (click-through / gravity / stroll)… : Option Default Description Click through transparent areas On Passes clicks on transparent pixels to windows underneath Gravity landing Off Falls onto the taskbar / Dock on release and bounces off edges Stroll occasionally Off Walks short distances along the bottom of the screen now and then Touch reactions On Responses to hovering, head pats, and clicks Eyes follow the global cursor On Tracks the pointer even when outside the character window Show AI replies in bubble On Displays replies in the speech bubble beside her # Adding a New Action Add an entry to ACTIONS in actions.ts : id (lowercase snake_case), label (UI locale key), category , dur , trigger , and tracks; add the Chinese label under packages/i18n/src/locales/zh/ui/ and the matching English label under en .
