d: Speech input, wake word, the character's voice
h: Real-Time TTS Engine (Default: Edge Online TTS)
Read AI Replies Aloud (On by Default)
x: Settings entry point: Settings → General → Voice . # Voice Input Hold to talk : Hold the microphone button in the input bar, or hold F2 in the chat window; press Esc to cancel. If recognition is not configured yet (neither a local model downloaded nor a cloud provider set up), the microphone and hands-free buttons stay hidden from the input bar: open the + menu in the input box and click Set up voice input… to configure it; pressing F2 or the hands-free shortcut also opens Voice settings directly. Hands-free voice : Ctrl/⌘+Shift+H , or toggle from the voice menu on Nomi's toolbar. Automatically detects when you start and stop speaking with adjustable sensitivity (Sensitive / Balanced / Conservative). Downloading Silero VAD improves detection accuracy; otherwise, basic energy-based detection is used. Interrupt read-aloud when you start speaking : Speaking while Nomi is reading aloud immediately stops playback. Auto-send after recognition : On by default; when off, recognized text is placed into the input box so you can edit it first. Recognition engines : Local whisper.cpp (offline, recommended): Engine and models download on demand, displaying license info before download and verifying SHA-256 afterward; larger models improve accuracy at the cost of disk space and latency. OpenAI-compatible service : Uses a saved third-party provider or a custom base URL (such as a local whisper.cpp server), calling /audio/transcriptions . Doubao Streaming ASR 2.0 (Volcengine, bring your own API Key): Streams audio in real time for recognition and is billed by the provider; requires activation in the Volcengine console first. Can be configured to fall back to local whisper.cpp if cloud recognition fails. Cloud recognition asks for your consent before uploading audio; when Only local models can read files is enabled, recordings cannot be sent to the cloud. # Wake Word (Experimental, Off by Default) When enabled, speaking the wake word starts listening; anything spoken immediately after it is handled directly as a command. Defaults to the active character pack's wake word ( Hello, Nomi for the official pack) and can be customized to 2–8 Chinese characters or words in English. Wake-word detection always runs locally via whisper.cpp without uploading audio and requires downloading the local engine and model first; when enabled, the microphone listens continuously in the background. # Nomi's Voice Voice playback consists of two parts: pre-recorded prompt clips and a real-time TTS engine . If a line has a pre-recorded clip, that clip plays; otherwise, it is handed to the real-time engine. When the engine is set to None or synthesis fails, only text is shown. # Character Prompt Voice (On by Default) 96 pre-recorded Chinese prompt clips for Nomi's common lines (greetings, reminders, voice toggles, etc.) are bundled with the installer under characters/nomi/voice/zh/ . Plays only when the UI language is Chinese, Nomi is not muted, and Character prompt voice is enabled. For lines with variables (such as You missed N reminders while you were away ), the bubble shows the full text while the voice plays a fixed phrasing; the same line plays at most once every 1.5 seconds. # Real-Time TTS Engine (Default: Edge Online TTS) Option Description Edge online TTS (default) Defaults to Xiaoyi ( zh-CN-XiaoyiNeural ), rate -5%; requires internet access None (text only) Disables speech synthesis; pre-recorded prompt clips are unaffected Azure Speech / OpenAI TTS Not yet wired up; selecting them produces no audio and shows text only Edge TTS uses the online service backing Microsoft Edge's Read aloud feature— it is not an official public Microsoft API and may stop working in the future. If you do not want spoken text sent to Microsoft, set the engine to None . Voices and rate : The voice list is fetched online and filtered to Chinese voices, falling back to a few built-in voices if unavailable. Speech rate ranges from -50% to +50% and applies to both character lines and AI replies. Preview synthesizes a sample sentence using unsaved settings; Check connection synthesizes a short test phrase and reports latency. Code, URLs, HTML, and Markdown syntax are stripped before speaking; long text is split into sentences and prefetched sequentially during playback. When offline, timed out (15 seconds), or if the service changes, playback fails silently and shows text only; consecutive failures show Real-time TTS is temporarily unreachable in Settings. # Read AI Replies Aloud (On by Default) When Read AI replies aloud is on and the real-time TTS engine is available, Nomi reads replies in Nomi chats aloud as they stream; agent tabs and delegated turns are not read aloud. Code blocks, inline code, thinking blocks, tables, and URLs are skipped; each reply reads only the first ~300 characters (aligned to full sentences). Sending a new message, stopping generation, switching or creating a conversation, or holding push-to-talk interrupts playback immediately. # Privacy The app never saves recordings or keeps audio history. Local whisper.cpp recognition (including wake-word detection) writes the current clip temporarily to the system temp directory ( cd-asr-*/in.wav , readable only by the current user) for the engine to read and deletes it on completion, error, or cancellation; all other recordings are processed strictly in memory. The local engine is completely offline and never uploads audio; online recognition sends audio to the selected provider, logs every call to the audit log, and is governed by the provider's data retention policy. API keys for cloud recognition are encrypted in the OS secure storage and are not saved if secure storage is unavailable. # Implementation UI: packages/voice (recording, VAD, wake word, settings panel); Nomi playback and lip-sync in packages/renderer/src/mascot/tts/audioPlayback.ts ; pre-recorded clips in packages/renderer/src/mascot/voice/promptClips.ts ; reply sentence splitting in packages/ai-chat/src/services/replySpeech.ts . Core: recognition in apps/desktop-go/internal/core/voice ( whisper.go , cloudasr.go , volc.go ), TTS in internal/core/tts (the Edge client in tts/edge/ is built in and does not require Microsoft Edge to be installed). Pre-recorded clip generation script: scripts/voice/gen.py (requires pip install edge-tts and ffmpeg ).

d: Notch-style notices on macOS
h: When the Workbench Is on Screen
x: When Nomi is not on the desktop, Nomi notifications appear in a Dynamic Island style centered at the top of the screen: expanding from the notch on Macs with a notch, or appearing as a centered top pill on other displays. Click it to open and focus the chat window; press Esc or click the close button to dismiss the entire island. Things waiting for you (agent permission prompts, sandbox blocks, tasks awaiting approval or review, Nomi confirmation requests) stay on the island with action buttons so you can allow or deny right there. Clicking an item (or its Open button) opens the chat window and jumps straight to it: task details for tasks, the agent tab for agent requests, or the main chat for Nomi confirmations. Settings: Settings → General → Notifications / Dynamic Island . Enable Dynamic Island notifications : On by default on macOS; optional top pill on Windows / Linux, off by default. When turned off, alerts fall back to system notifications while Nomi is not on the desktop. Notification types (individually toggleable): Things waiting for you (on by default; see below), Proactive AI messages (proactive chats, daily briefings, etc.), Agents (one notice on completion, confirmation needed, or error, with no mid-run progress updates), and Schedule reminders (due reminders and scheduled task results). Always use top pill : Centers at the top edge instead of attaching to the notch. Show a preview notification lets you test the layout. # Where Notifications Go Reminders, scheduled task results, proactive chats, agent updates, and usage budget alerts each appear in only one place: Nomi is on the desktop : Uses her speech bubble only (reminders show as reminder cards), with neither Dynamic Island nor system notifications. Nomi is closed or hidden : Uses the Dynamic Island; if the Dynamic Island is off, unsupported on the platform, or disabled for that source, falls back to a system notification (clicking opens the chat window). Do-not-disturb hours ( Settings → Knowledge Memory → Schedule → Do Not Disturb ): Nothing pops up, and reminders queue until the window ends. macOS Focus has no public API and cannot be detected automatically. Notifies once when things finish: no progress bars, periodic summaries, or N tasks still running broadcasts; scheduled task results are always written to the chat window. When the Nomi workbench is on screen : Shows only Things waiting for you and Alerts (see next section); suppressed notifications do not fall back to system notifications. # When the Workbench Is on Screen Each notification is classified first and routed through a single policy check ( Classify / ShouldShow in internal/core/island/policy.go , shared by both the Dynamic Island and fallback system notifications): Category Includes Workbench off-screen Workbench on-screen (viewing another session / unfocused) Viewing the notification's own session Progress In progress, periodic summaries, stalled checks Suppress (removed) Suppress Suppress Completion Agent finished, turn finished waiting for reply, scheduled task results Show Suppress Suppress Other Proactive AI messages, daily briefings Show Suppress Suppress Waiting for you Agent permissions, questions, plan approvals, sandbox blocks, Nomi OKs Show Show Suppress (card is already in chat) Alert Failures / errors, due reminders, persistent task notices, budget alerts Show Show Suppress (errors appear in chat) Workbench on screen means the chat window is visible and not minimized. Platforms do not expose whether a window is occluded by other windows, so an occluded window still counts as on screen. Viewing the notification's own session means the chat window is on screen, Nomi is focused, and the active tab matches the notification's tab (Nomi confirmations and questions map to the main chat). Reminders, usage alerts, and agents in external terminals do not belong to any session and are never suppressed by this rule. The Waiting for you list follows the same rule: items belonging to the session you are currently viewing stay off the island and appear (within 5 seconds) once you switch tabs or leave the window; persistent task items belong to no session and always show. When Nomi is on the desktop, she still uses her speech bubble unaffected by this rule; do-not-disturb hours and per-type toggles still apply. # Things Waiting for You Listed on the island until handled (shown regardless of whether Nomi is on the desktop and even during do-not-disturb hours, since they block progress). Press Esc or click the close button in the top-right corner of the list to hide it temporarily: the items remain pending and can still be handled in chat or on the Tasks page, and they reappear alongside any new item that arrives. Clicked buttons re-enable after 8 seconds if no result arrives. Items handled elsewhere (answering a permission prompt in a tab, confirming in chat, or acting on the Tasks page) disappear from the island immediately; agents delegated from Nomi chat return results to the conversation for follow-up (reply or accept) and no longer stay on the island as Waiting for review . Buttons share the same entry point as chat and Tasks—acting anywhere clears all places together: Source Island buttons Agent tool permission Allow / Deny Nomi, Claude Code, Codex, or ACP waiting for your answer Open (answer in chat) Agent plan awaiting approval Approve auto-edit files (or Execute this plan ) / Ask step by step / Keep editing Agent blocked by sandbox Allow for this session / Always allow / Deny; protected folders allow only Deny or Open Settings Persistent task awaiting approval Approve / Reject Persistent task configuration changed Handled, continue / Give up Persistent task you took over Mark done / Hand back Persistent task awaiting review Accept / Open (send back requires feedback) Persistent task needing verification It took effect / It didn't / Open Nomi confirmation (desktop actions, commands, MCP, handoff, folder scope) Allow / Deny; actions requiring full review offer Open only More info needed or reauthorization required Open Open opens the chat window. A permission request on a task-dispatched agent tab is the same item as that task's Awaiting approval and is listed only once under the task. Agent permission requests already in the waiting list do not trigger a separate Confirmation needed notice. A single item renders as one large pill; multiple items show a header row ( N waiting for you ) followed by up to 4 visible items with scrolling for more. When a regular notification arrives, it stacks at the top of the list and collapses after a few seconds. # Appearance Macs with a notch : The top edge attaches flush to the top of the screen, extending downward out of the notch with rounded bottom corners only; content (icon, title, buttons) sits below the notch's bottom edge. Notch mode is always solid black. Screens without a notch / forced pill : Translucent dark floating pill (440 px wide, 64 px tall for a single item) with four rounded corners and a drop shadow. Left side shows Nomi's icon (or the agent's icon for agent events) with a bottom-right badge: spinner while running, green checkmark on completion, red exclamation on failure, amber exclamation when waiting for you, and pink heart for messages. Right side shows action buttons for waiting items or a close button for notifications. Window height tracks content dynamically (the page reports height changes to the core, which resizes the window), growing with the list so it never holds an invisible transparent area that blocks clicks underneath. Expands and collapses over ~0.36 seconds with no bounce; transitions are disabled when the system Reduce motion setting is on. Does not steal focus, stays visible across all desktop Spaces, and renders content strictly as plain text. # Implementation apps/desktop-go/internal/core/island : notification routing in notify.go , pending list in pending.go , layout geometry in geometry.go (pure functions with unit tests), HTML view in island.html (embedded into the binary); window management in internal/shell/wailsshell . Pending-item sources and button wiring: apps/desktop-go/island_pending.go (refreshes on tab events, task changes, and confirmation prompt open/close, with a 5-second fallback poll). Details for agent permission prompts are tracked by the orchestrator ( cli/harness/pending_perms.go ). Page-to-core postMessage signals: nomi:island:size: height resizes the window, nomi:island:act:{id, action} handles button clicks, nomi:island:open opens chat, and nomi:island:hidden signals hide completion. On macOS, the island window is a true borderless window ( MacWindowCornerTypeSquare in Wails): Wails' default frameless window retains titlebar styling, causing macOS to push it below the menu bar with rounded corners and detach it from the notch. In dev builds ( pnpm dev ), Settings → Debug previews every style on the real island: each notification type and waiting-list sample (1, 3, or 7 scrolling items, etc.). Samples use island.debug , which the core accepts only when NOMI_DEV_VIEWS is set; clicking a sample button simply removes the sample. Notch presence is inferred from built-in display + menu bar height , falling back to pill style if uncertain. For debugging, CD_ISLAND_SIMULATE_NOTCH=1 simulates a notch on any platform.

d: Themes, app icons, sidebar, shortcuts, language, accessibility
h: My Themes (Custom Themes and Theme Packs)
x: Theme and app icon settings live under Settings → General → General → Appearance . # Themes Options: Light (default for new users), Dark , Sunset , Warm ink , Graphite , Cream , Cool mist , Follow system (dark when the OS is dark, light when light), and Image theme . The chat window, settings, onboarding, and title bar switch together; users who already picked a theme keep their existing choice. # Image Theme After selecting Image theme , the image picker, Frosted glass , and Mask opacity appear beneath the theme cards: A crisp background image fills the window across chat, sidebar, right panel, settings, and dialogs. Frosted glass adjusts the background-sampling blur of the global overlay mask without scaling or blurring the underlying image itself, keeping text and controls sharp. Mask opacity adjusts only the overlay mask, not the image: higher values make the mask more opaque and the image subtler. Setting Frosted glass to 0px disables blur. The theme card previews the mask effect in real time. Uses the built-in preset image ( apps/desktop-go/assets/backgrounds/nomi-preset.jpg ) by default, and can be replaced with your own image. Chosen images are cached so they still load after restart even if the original file is moved or deleted; changing the image preserves your blur and opacity settings. Defaults to 0px frosted glass and 50% mask opacity; Reset to default restores the preset image and these defaults without leaving Image theme. Image theme uses the Graphite palette; delegation cards, tasks, and library panels also use transparent surfaces. # My Themes (Custom Themes and Theme Packs) Create your own palette or import theme packs shared by others. To the right of the Themes heading are the Follow system toggle, New theme , and Import theme pack ; custom themes appear in the same card grid as built-in themes, sorted first (with a palette icon before the name). When Follow system is on, Nomi switches between Light and Dark with the OS; clicking any theme card or turning the toggle off locks in a fixed theme (stopping on whichever version is currently active). Import theme pack opens a modal: drag a theme pack in, or click to select a file via the system picker (canceling does nothing). Drag-and-drop supports files up to 12 MB; use the picker for larger files. Download template in the modal saves a dual light/dark template ( nomi-theme-template.nomitheme.json ) ready to edit and re-import. New theme opens a right-side drawer seeded with the current theme's colors and four base inputs: Accent , Background , Surface (cards and panels), and Text . You can also paste multiple #rrggbb values into Paste a palette to fill them in that order. Remaining colors (hover, active, borders, muted text, pressed buttons, etc.) are derived automatically. For single-variant themes, a dark background treats the theme as dark mode so window chrome and status colors (success, warning, error) follow dark conventions; a light background follows light mode. Enabling Separate light and dark versions lets you configure light and dark palettes independently so the theme switches with the OS appearance; the counterpart starts from the default Light or Dark theme using your accent color. Advanced: adjust individual colors lists overridable tokens by group—leave a field blank to keep the derived value. Supports #rrggbb , rgb() , hsl() , and oklch() . Background image adds an image to the theme (PNG, JPEG, or WebP, up to 15 MB; PNG/JPEG images exceeding 2560px on the long edge are downscaled), with Frosted glass and Mask opacity controls that make UI panels translucent, just like Image theme. While editing, the entire window live-previews the version you are editing (including its background image), reverting if you cancel; saving switches to the theme and syncs all windows (including desktop character speech bubbles). Contrast checks list contrast ratios for body text, muted text, button text, and links, flagging any pair below 4.5:1 . Accent colors are nudged automatically if button text or links lack contrast; if the accent itself falls below 3:1 against the background, it is adjusted just enough to pass for non-text elements like switches and accent lines. Body text color is never altered automatically. Selecting a custom theme reveals Edit (in the same drawer), Export theme pack , and Delete beneath the cards. Deleting the active theme reverts to the default theme. Up to 100 custom themes can be saved. A theme pack without a background image is a single JSON file ( .nomitheme.json ); with a background image, it is a zip archive ( .nomitheme ) containing theme.json and background.png / .jpg / .webp . theme.json : name can be a plain string or an object keyed by language ( zh / en ); base is light or dark . seeds can omit any subset of keys to inherit them from the base theme; values must be #rgb or #rrggbb . tokens is optional and directly overrides derived values, accepting only color tokens listed in packages/ui/src/themeTokens.ts ; values may only use hex, rgb() , rgba() , hsl() , hsla() , or oklch() . variants is optional and holds only the counterpart opposite to base ( seeds / tokens as above); when present, the theme follows the OS appearance. background applies only inside a .nomitheme zip; image is the filename inside the archive, blur ranges from 0 to 40 , and opacity ranges from 0.05 to 1 . format : exports as 1 when using only name / base / seeds / tokens , or 2 when using variants or background . Older app versions do not recognize format 2 and reject importing it. theme.json is capped at 64 KB and the image at 15 MB. Invalid syntax, unlisted tokens, disallowed CSS functions (such as url(...) or var(...) ), or extra files in the zip cause the entire pack to be rejected. # App Icon App icon under Appearance : Sunset (default), Cream , Ink . The window, taskbar / Dock, and tray icons update immediately; static icons in installers, executables, and Finder / Start Menu keep the default Ink icon. The macOS menu bar tray icon always uses a monochrome template icon. Icon assets are documented in Brand Guidelines . # Sidebar On the left of the sidebar is a fixed navigation rail: Chats , Tasks , and Library sit at the top (the first icon aligns with the top row of the session panel; toggle the session panel with the button on the left of the title bar). When agents are installed, all endpoints ( All , Nomi, and each agent) appear vertically below a divider so one click filters sessions by endpoint. d: Background download; installs in place and relaunches when you confirm
x: Settings entry point: Settings → About (also reachable from the version card at the top of General ). The page contains only the version card—check for updates, project homepage / changelog / recent updates / feedback—with Update settings in a secondary dialog (automatic checks and showing release notes after updating); the GitHub Star prompt at the bottom can be dismissed. Installed builds check for updates roughly 15 seconds after launch and every 3 hours thereafter. You can disable Check for updates on launch and periodically in Update settings , or click Check for updates manually anytime. When a new version is found, Nomi downloads the installer for your platform in the background and shows progress in Settings. If a release was just published and your platform's installer has not finished uploading yet, Nomi prompts you to check again later. Once downloaded, Nomi displays Update downloaded, restart to install , shows Restart to update at the right of the title bar (when outside Settings) and bottom-left of Settings, and Restart and install on the About page (with a confirmation dialog). Your confirmation is always required before installing—Nomi never installs updates silently on quit. After you confirm: macOS : Nomi exits, swaps the new version into its existing location ( Nomi.app in Applications), and relaunches automatically without requiring drag-and-drop. Only when Nomi is not in a writable location (e.g., running directly from a .dmg , running quarantined from Downloads, or inside a non-writable folder) does it open the new .dmg for you to drag into Applications. Windows : Runs the installer silently in the background to overwrite the installation and relaunches automatically without showing a wizard. Linux : AppImage replaces itself in place and relaunches; .deb packages hand off to the system software installer. Checks or downloads with no response for 90 seconds cancel automatically and report a failure; failures at any step specify which step failed and change the button to Retry . On relaunch after updating, if Show release notes after update is enabled (on by default), Nomi displays the release notes for the new version; you can reopen them anytime from About → Recent updates . Auto-update is disabled when running from source, and Settings notes this. After an update finishes installing and relaunches, Nomi deletes used installers from the cache directory ( dmg , zip , exe , AppImage , deb ) along with incomplete partial downloads. Installers for versions not yet installed are kept to avoid re-downloading. Nomi never deletes the currently running binary, files in your Downloads folder, or any user data: the macOS .zip used for in-place replacement is deleted right after successful extraction, while Windows installers and system-opened .dmg / .deb files wait until the new version launches because the installation process still needs them. # Implementation Update feed: latest-go.json on this project's GitHub Releases (per-platform installer URL, size, SHA-256, and release notes; macOS entries also include an update field pointing to the -mac.zip used for in-place replacement); downloads are verified by SHA-256. macOS in-place swap ( swap_unix.go ): Extracts the .zip into a hidden staging directory next to Nomi.app , verifies a valid signature, matching Bundle ID, and matching Team ID with the running app, then uses a small standalone helper script to wait for Nomi to exit, swap the new Nomi.app into place (restoring the old one on failure), and relaunch it. Windows runs the NSIS installer with /S --updated --force-run ( packaging/windows/installer.nsi ). Code: apps/desktop-go/internal/core/updates ( service.go for scheduling and state, github.go for download and install, releasenotes.go for release notes); the manifest is generated by apps/desktop-go/packaging/update-manifest.py . See Release Process .

Product name / appId stay in the host brand and are never taken from the pack. displayName , systemPromptIdentity and greetings are required ( greetings may be empty — validation warns). displayName is the full name, used where the UI first names the character (「你好，我是 Nomi·诺米」); shortName (optional, defaults to displayName ) is used for later mentions (「显示 Nomi」「Nomi 大小」). At run time lines fall back to the primary locale. Validation warns when a non-primary locale misses keys present in zh . Legacy copy/ lang .json ( displayName , wakePhrase , systemPromptIdentity ) is migrated with a warning. # Modes manifest.assets.mode Required assets Notes rive (default) rive/character.riv Primary path; sprite strongly recommended as fallback sprite sprite/ layered rig May be primary or fallback static static/character.webp (or png) No .riv , no 43 actions required # Rive Field Default (Nomi) Override Artboard Nomi-full manifest.rive.artboard State machine NomiFull manifest.rive.stateMachine File rive/character.riv manifest.assets.rive Native motion clip names: see contract.json → rive.nativeMotions . x: Third-party providers (API relays and model platforms) can put a button on their website so users can add the provider to Nomi's gateway with one click. Both integration methods stop at a confirmation dialog inside Nomi: nothing is written until the user clicks Confirm . Method Link Best for Key in link? A Direct import nomi://provider/import?v=1 data=… Relay one-click fill buttons; takes only a few lines of template code Yes B Authorized link nomi://provider/connect?v=1 issuer=… Platforms with user accounts willing to add an auth page and a key-exchange endpoint No (exchanged via PKCE auth code) Industry references: Cherry Studio's cherrystudio://providers/api-keys?v=1 data= base64 (Method A is compatible with its fields), CC Switch's ccswitch://v1/import , base64-payload MCP install links in Cursor / VS Code, and OpenRouter's PKCE flow (Method B). # A: Direct import data uses base64url ( +/ replaced with -_ , = padding optional); standard base64 is also accepted. JSON: Also compatible with Cherry Studio's flat format: { name , baseUrl , apiKey , type ? } . When type is anthropic , baseUrl maps to messages ; gemini maps to gemini ; everything else maps to chat . Relay template example (for the Chat link field in New API, etc.): # B: Authorized connect Place the link nomi://provider/connect?v=1 issuer=https://example.com on your page ( issuer must be an https origin with no path). Users can also initiate this by entering the domain in Nomi's Add third-party provider dialog. Nomi fetches https://example.com/.well-known/nomi-provider.json : Both endpoints must use https , and their hosts must match the issuer host or one of its subdomains. After the user confirms inside Nomi, Nomi opens the system browser to: After the user signs in and approves on the third-party provider's page, the page redirects to nomi://provider/callback?code={code} state={state} (or error=access_denied state=… on rejection). Nomi matches state to the pending session (valid for 10 minutes, single-use) and sends a POST application/x-www-form-urlencoded request to token_endpoint : The endpoint returns { api_key : sk-… , name ?: … , urls ?: {…}, models ?: […] } ( key / access_token are also accepted). Any urls in the token response override matching protocol entries from the manifest. Nomi opens the same confirmation dialog as Method A and saves the provider once confirmed. # Nomi's handling rules Always confirm first : The confirmation dialog shows the name, source (A: Link , source website cannot be verified; B: issuer domain), protocol URLs, masked key, and model count; step 1 of Method B (opening the browser to authorize) also requires confirmation. URLs : Only https URLs without embedded credentials and not pointing to localhost or a LAN address are accepted (add local services manually in Settings). Resolving the authorization host : Follows the same rules as the gateway connecting upstream—hosts resolving to localhost / LAN are rejected (error code private_host ), proxy fake-IPs ( 198.18.0.0/15 ) are allowed for domain names, and resolution failures report network . Show only verifiable sources : Method A states only Web link; unable to verify which website it came from and does not display the link's self-reported site name or homepage; Method B displays the issuer domain (which Nomi connected to directly). Populate models after adding : When a link omits models, Nomi runs a probe with the newly saved key after saving and enables chat models according to the standard add-provider rules. Update if existing : If an existing third-party provider already has one of the link's URLs (ignoring trailing / ), Nomi updates that entry—adding the new key (skipping duplicates) and filling in any unset protocol URLs and models; otherwise it creates a new provider. All URLs in the link must share the same origin (scheme + host + port) as that provider's existing URLs: if another domain is included, Nomi creates a new provider containing only the link's new key so existing keys are never sent to the newly added domain (#249). Limits : Total link length ≤ 16 KB; name ≤ 64 characters; key 8–512 printable characters; up to 200 models; at most 5 pending confirmations at once, expiring after 10 minutes, with identical payloads deduplicated. No key leaks in logs : Because links may contain keys, logs record only the link type and never the raw link; keys stay in the core, and views only receive masked values. Cold start : If the app is launched via a link while closed, the core holds it until the chat window mounts and fetches it ( providerLink.list ); already-open windows receive it via providerLink.changed . # Implementation locations Parsing, validation, PKCE: apps/desktop-go/internal/core/providerlink/link.go ; flow and state (pending links, auth sessions, fetching manifests, exchanging keys): service.go in the same directory. The host only passes incoming nomi:// links to it (storing them on cold start). Contract: providerLink.list / accept / reject / connect , event providerLink.changed ( packages/contract/src/app/shell.ts ), handlers in apps/desktop-go/internal/core/shellhandlers/providerlink.go . UI: packages/ai-chat/src/components/ProviderLink .

d: How the Go core, the Wails shell and the views fit together
x: Nomi is a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo. The desktop application lives in apps/desktop-go (Go core + Wails v3 shell), and the UI is built with React 19 + Vite, with its build artifacts embedded into the Go binary. As of 2.2.0, the Electron edition (Node core) has been removed. # Processes and Windows The composition root is main.go and *_wiring.go : they instantiate services, register contract procedures, and launch the shell. internal/shell defines the shell interface, and wailsshell/ is the only package that depends on Wails; business modules ( internal/core ) do not depend on Wails. Views access the core exclusively through the app contract: the page URL fragment carries ws://127.0.0.1: port and a per-window one-time token provided by the host. Each view's services/api.ts calls installGoHostTransport to configure the WebSocket transport (this is the only file in each view package allowed to select the transport and create the client; ESLint blocks all other locations). The core identifies the caller's surface by its token, and the contract guard enforces the surfaces and dangerous flags declared on each procedure. Window-scoped events are registered in the contract's eventSurfaces , and the transport layer filters subscriptions by the caller's surface. The contract's procedure table and types are generated from the TS contract ( packages/contract ) into internal/contract/gen via node scripts/go-contract/gen.mjs (CI checks for drift). Handlers are organized by domain under internal/core/ domain handlers . Native paths of dropped files do not go through the contract: the host captures them from native drag-and-drop events ( WindowFilesDropped ). The desktop character window submits them directly, while the chat window matches them by filename ( nomi:host-files ); views cannot pick arbitrary paths. chat-asset:// and character-pack:// are served through the asset server gateway /__scheme/ scheme /... . When Go serves pages ( internal/shell/viewpage ), it rewrites the CSP and injects the Wails runtime. # Packages Location Role apps/desktop-go/internal/core Business modules: agent orchestration, usage tracking, gateway provider store, desktop capabilities, knowledge base, long-term memory, scheduler, local models, extensions, voice, updates, diagnostics, etc., plus contract handlers apps/desktop-go/internal/ai AI runtime: providers and routing, LLM client, MCP bridge, AI facade apps/desktop-go/internal/gateway Unified gateway: request IR and streaming translation across Messages / Responses / Chat / Gemini apps/desktop-go/internal/clisdk Agent plugin contract and shared session drivers ( acp / stream-json / app-server / exec ); see docs/development/coding-agents.md apps/desktop-go/internal/cliplugins Built-in agent plugins ( claude / codex / gemini / grok / dsh ): launch injection, permission modes, official accounts, history scanning, etc. packages/renderer Desktop character window shell: transparent window, speech bubbles, toolbar, context menu, and a thin adapter layer ( src/avatar , src/ai ) connecting contract events to avatar-runtime packages/avatar-runtime Character engine (browser-only): Rive / sprite / static backends, expression and motion drivers, hit zones and interactions, lip-sync consumption; see character-pack for character packs; standalone dev page at pnpm --filter @nomi-ai/avatar-runtime demo packages/ai-chat Chat window: conversations, settings, onboarding, and feature panels packages/ai-sdk-client View-side AI client ( ClientAIClient ), shared per-window contract transport, and React hooks packages/contract API contract between views and core (procedures, events, schemas, version handshake, WebSocket transport); see contract.md packages/character-contract Character pack contract: schemas, validation, and migration for manifest, persona, mapping, and locales; see character-pack packages/cli-catalog Manifests and UI metadata for built-in agents (pure data, consumed by views) packages/ui Design tokens, 4 themes, shared components, and view locale adapter packages/i18n ( @nomi-ai/i18n ) Unified multilingual dictionary and runtime, organized by language / project / module ( packages/i18n/src/locales ); Go core embeds a copy; see i18n.md for pnpm check:i18n + keepZh packages/voice Voice input, VAD, and wake word packages/types Shared types and brand constants # Agents and Unified Gateway See coding-agents.md and gateway.md for details. Plugins : internal/clisdk defines the contract (manifest, capability interfaces, session drivers, multi-option permission replies) and the four session drivers; internal/cliplugins contains the five built-in plugins. Only built-in plugins are supported (user-added external CLIs are no longer supported); manifests and UI metadata for views live in @nomi-ai/cli-catalog . Orchestration : internal/core/cli/harness manages tabs, persistence, sources (official / third-party), the official account catalog, recycling, and upgrade restarts. Protocol details live in the drivers, while per-CLI parsing (streaming, history transcripts, model catalogs, slash-command layouts) lives in each plugin. Gateway layers : On the request path, requests go through provider adapters ( providers/ ) and model adapters ( models/ : catalog, family rules, request rules, error fixers). On the response path, responses go through canonicalization ( canonical/ , filling fields and detecting completion against protocol spec tables in spec/ ), the protocol bridge, and client adapters ( clients/ ). Route planning lives in route/ . Provider storage : Third-party providers and API keys are stored only in the gateway store ( userData/gateway/store.json , internal/core/gwstore ). Nomi chat, agent-tools , and summary resolve models through the gateway. Delegation : Nomi can asynchronously hand off tasks to agent tabs ( delegate_to_cli , background by default). By default, edits happen in-place in the working directory (parallel tasks in the same repo coordinate by file and priority); a worktree is created only when a different base branch is specified. Delegated tabs and sessions are visible only inside Nomi, and identical delegations reuse sessions. See coding-agents.md and security.md (Python OS sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec / Linux bwrap ). Tab bindings : Before launching a CLI process for a third-party tab, a nomi-tab- token is issued and registered with the gateway (tab, generation, model, thinking depth). The gateway resolves the model from the binding and tags request logs with the tab ID; the binding is invalidated when the process exits or the tab closes. Diagnostics : internal/core/diagnostics manages toggles, CLI subprocess I/O recording, and diagnostic bundle export. Gateway tracing assigns a trace ID per request ( x-nomi-trace-id response header). # Key Conventions Data : All data is stored under userData (macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Nomi , Windows %APPDATA%\Nomi , Linux ~/.config/Nomi ) in feature-specific directories; API keys are stored in the OS keychain. Views never store business data in WebView localStorage (only UI preferences): chat sessions live in the core's userData/conversations/ ( internal/core/convstore , contract conversations.* , see chat.md ), so dev and packaged builds share the same data regardless of page origin. On first launch, data is migrated from the legacy Electron directory ( internal/migrate ). Network and commands : Outbound requests pass through the gateway's network guard, which blocks localhost/private IP addresses and pins DNS resolutions. Command execution escapes arguments, and private files are written with mode 0600 . Logging : Views use createLogger from @nomi-ai/ui rather than console.log ; Go core uses the logger from internal/core/services . UI : CSS Modules + var(--cd-*) design tokens; feature panels are lazy-loaded; desktop character Rive scenes are loaded on demand. i18n : Package @nomi-ai/i18n ; stable keys follow the project.module.message format; raw Chinese strings cannot be used as keys. Verified by pnpm check:i18n (including keys referenced in Go source and embedded JSON); see i18n.md .

d: Procedures, events and transport between the views and the core
x: All calls and pushed events between the views ( packages/ai-chat , packages/renderer ) and the core go through the app contract. The contract is defined once in packages/contract (using Zod schemas), from which the Go core's procedure table, types, and unimplemented stubs are generated. # What Is in the Contract Item Location Description Procedures packages/contract/src/app/{ai,shell,coding,knowledge,media,mascot}.ts Dot-separated names ( appIcon.set ); query / mutation / stream ( stream also defines a per-chunk schema) Events Same as above, events Pushed from the core to views; delivered only after a view subscribes via api.on(name, fn) Business error codes Each domain's errors E.g., KB_EMPTY , SCHED_NOT_FOUND ; generated into Go's gen.Errors Version appContract.version Handshaken via meta.version before the client's first call; a major mismatch fails calls with VERSION_MISMATCH ; Go returns ContractVersion from internal/contract/frames.go Procedure access control is declared directly on the definition and enforced by guards on both sides (Go: guard in internal/contract/frames.go ): surfaces : Allowed calling surfaces ( chat / mascot / settings ); omitted means all surfaces; mismatches return FORBIDDEN . dangerous: true : Accepts only trusted callers (procedures that modify files, execute commands, or touch secrets). The caller's surface is determined by the host: each window gets a one-time token, the core maps token - surface , and if the surface claimed in the subprotocol does not match, the handshake is rejected ( internal/contract/websocket.go ). Views cannot choose their own identity. # Transport When creating a window, the Go host passes ws://127.0.0.1: port and that window's token in the URL fragment ( #ws=... token=... ; fragments are never sent to the server). Before building the client, each view's services/api.ts calls installGoHostTransport(surface) ( @nomi-ai/ai-sdk-client ), which installs the WebSocket transport ( createWebSocketClientTransport , accepting only 127.0.0.1 ) when configuration is present. A window has only one contract session, shared between api and ClientAIClient in AIProvider . Outside a Nomi window (tests, browser preview), no transport is installed: hasTransport() is false, and calls fail with BRIDGE_MISSING . Wire protocol: the client sends req / abort / sub / unsub , and the server replies with res / chunk / end / err / event ( packages/contract/src/protocol.ts ). Only JSON values and Uint8Array (base64-encoded over WebSocket per wire.ts ) are supported; Date / Map / Set cannot cross the wire. When a window closes, the host revokes its token and closes the connection. After a disconnect, the client reconnects with backoff and restores event subscriptions. Validation: by default, the client validates inputs, results, every chunk, and every event against schemas. Production builds of the views ( import.meta.env.PROD ) enable lean validation in services/api.ts ( setLeanValidation({ events: APP_HIGH_FREQUENCY_EVENTS, procedures: APP_LARGE_RESULT_PROCEDURES }) ): streaming chunks, high-frequency events (streaming output, cursor, window movement, full messages pushed at turn end), chunk/event frame envelopes, and results of large-result procedures (full conversation messages, full git diffs, workspace file trees) skip validation; inputs, other call results, final stream results, and other events are still validated as usual. Schemas for these skipped events and procedures must not use default or transform (since raw values are returned when validation is bypassed). # Adding a Procedure Add the definition in the corresponding domain file packages/contract/src/app/ domain .ts (input/output schemas, surfaces , dangerous ). Generate the Go side: Do not manually edit the generated files internal/contract/gen/{procedures_gen,types_gen}.go or contract.schema.json . Implement in Go: place handlers by domain under internal/core/ domain handlers ( shellhandlers , codinghandlers , knowledgehandlers , mediahandlers , mascothandlers ), register with r.Call(name, ...) / r.Stream(name, ...) , and wire them in the composition root ( main.go / *_wiring.go ). Unregistered procedures are backed by stubs in internal/procs that return UNAVAILABLE , so views always receive an explicit error. Call from the view via api. domain . procedure (...) . Only services/api.ts may create clients or select transports (ESLint blocks other locations); shared packages ( @nomi-ai/ui , @nomi-ai/voice ) receive host capabilities through services/hostBackends/ domain .ts . Push events: on the Go side, use r.Emit(event, data) (all subscribed windows) or r.EmitTo(event, data, surface) (a specific surface); event names must first be declared in the contract. # Testing packages/contract/tests : schemas, procedure table snapshots, WebSocket transport, wire protocol. In views, use the in-process transport from @nomi-ai/contract/testing or the fake core in packages/ai-chat/tests/helpers/fakeApi.ts . In Go, internal/contract/*_test.go tests routing, guards, and WebSocket handshakes; each handlers package tests its own procedures.

d: Four protocols, routing, providers and models
x: Configure a third-party provider once, and both Nomi chat and all agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok, dsh) can use it. The gateway is a local HTTP service inside the Go core ( apps/desktop-go/internal/gateway ), listening exclusively on the loopback address at default port 18721 ( DefaultGatewayPort in internal/core/gwstore ). It accepts requests in each client's native protocol, decodes them into an intermediate representation (IR), dispatches them to upstream providers according to a route plan, and translates the response stream back into the client's protocol. # Ingress and Authentication Path Protocol .../messages , .../messages/count_tokens Anthropic Messages .../responses OpenAI Responses .../chat/completions OpenAI Chat Completions /v1beta/models/ model :generateContent / :streamGenerateContent / :countTokens Gemini GET .../models Model list (formatted per client protocol) GET /health , GET /metrics Health check, route quality snapshot (loopback-only, Host -validated, no token required) Validates the Host header (DNS rebinding protection); invalid hosts receive HTTP 421. Before launching a CLI for any third-party tab, the core issues a nomi-tab- token and registers a binding with the gateway (tab, generation, model, thinking depth). The CLI uses this token as its API key. The gateway resolves the model from the binding, tags request logs with the tab ID, and revokes the binding when the process exits or the tab closes ( internal/gateway/route/binding.go ). Missing or invalid tokens return an authentication error formatted for that protocol. All errors are encoded in the ingress protocol's error format ( internal/gateway/errors ) so clients display them properly. # Layers Directory Role upstream/ Ingress detection ( IngressFromPath ), upstream request fixups and retries request/ , ir/ Bidirectional conversion between each protocol's request and the protocol-agnostic IR providers/ Provider adapters: built-in presets and domain-matched specs (auth headers, endpoints, protocol capabilities) models/ Model catalog ( catalog.json , bundled offline), model family rules, request rules, effective model merging, model listing route/ Route planning: candidates (provider x key x protocol), binding resolution, native-protocol preference, failover, and fixers stream/ Upstream SSE decoding and event layer canonical/ , spec/ Field completion and completion detection according to each protocol's specification tables clients/ Client adapters: emit response streams matching each CLI's accepted format server/ HTTP server, protocol bridge ( bridge.go , passthrough or translate), first content-event commit ( commit.go ), session affinity, retries, tracing, usage accounting, metrics privacy/ Privacy mode: replaces secrets and other sensitive strings with placeholders before sending upstream, then restores them in responses net/ Address classification and outbound guard (blocks localhost/private IP addresses and pins DNS resolutions) probe/ Protocol probing when adding a provider media/ Image generation adapters and endpoints When fixing gateway or stream parsing issues, cover all four protocols and both passthrough and translation paths: first fix the issue in the shared layers ( stream/ event layer, canonical/ ), and only patch individual protocols when a shared fix is not possible, adding tests for each. # Providers and Models Third-party providers and API keys are stored solely in the gateway store userData/gateway/store.json ( internal/core/gwstore , keys encrypted); Nomi chat, agent-tools , and summary all resolve models via the gateway. Model capabilities (context/output limits, input modalities, tool calling, reasoning levels, sampling parameters) come from models/catalog.json , merged with provider-returned model lists and user overrides into effective models. The route plan selects an upstream protocol for each request: it passes through directly when the provider natively supports the ingress protocol, and translates otherwise. Multiple keys or protocols under the same provider are ranked by health samples with automatic failover. # Observability and Troubleshooting When diagnostics are enabled, the gateway writes per-request trace files ( userData/gateway/trace/*.json : ingress request, raw upstream response, diff of output sent to the client), and responses carry the x-nomi-trace-id header. GET /metrics : live snapshot of route quality and loss metrics. Usage is tallied from the stream per ingress protocol ( server/usagetap.go ) and written to the usage ledger. # Testing apps/desktop-go/internal/gateway/**/_test.go : per-layer unit tests, concurrency and race tests ( concurrency_test.go ), and long-context end-to-end tests ( context1m_e2e_test.go ). Use internal/mockllm for a mock upstream.

d: Plugins, session drivers, the orchestrator, permission levels

See features/coding-agents.md for user-facing documentation; this page covers the implementation. # Components Location Role packages/cli-catalog Manifests (ID, capability flags, session transport, permission mode mapping) and UI metadata for each built-in CLI, pure data; used by both views and core apps/desktop-go/internal/clisdk Plugin contract (manifest validation, capability interfaces, multi-option permission replies), external ACP plugins, subprocess launch ( launch/ ), and JSON-RPC ( rpc/ ) apps/desktop-go/internal/clisdk/drivers Four session drivers: acp , streamjson , appserver , exec apps/desktop-go/internal/cliplugins/ cli Built-in plugins: launch injection, permission modes, official account catalog, history transcript parsing, model catalog, slash commands; shared helpers live in shared/ apps/desktop-go/internal/core/cli/sandbox OS-level sandbox (macOS Seatbelt): per-tab profile generation, violation log monitoring, and classification; see security.md Agents apps/desktop-go/internal/core/cli/harness Orchestrator: tabs, persistence, source (official / third-party), permission queue, steer, idle recycling, upgrade restarts apps/desktop-go/internal/core/cli/accounts Official accounts: detect accounts logged in via terminal, import, sign in, switch (per-CLI isolated HOME / keychain) apps/desktop-go/internal/core/cli/delegate Nomi task delegation to agents ( delegate_to_cli ): in-place edits + per-file arbitration, worktree when targeting a different base branch, session reuse apps/desktop-go/internal/core/cli (other) CLI probing and versioning, install/update, session history, git operations (changes panel), slash command discovery, workspace files apps/desktop-go/internal/core/codinghandlers Agent-related contract procedures Tab messages are persisted in harness/tabs/ tab .json (up to 300 messages, with a 200 ms write debounce). The core keeps only the 6 most recently read tabs in memory ( MaxCachedTabMessages ), evicting older ones after synchronous operations complete; running/queued tabs, tabs with unflushed writes, and the active tab are exempt from eviction and reload from disk when read again. # Session Transports CLI Transport Fallback Claude Code stream-json exec Codex app-server (JSON-RPC) exec Gemini CLI acp — Grok acp exec dsh exec — Kimi Code acp — MiniMax acp — Antigravity CLI acp — Transports are declared via transport / fallbackTransport in packages/cli-catalog/src/ cli /manifest.ts . User-added external CLIs are no longer supported (the settings entry, cli.pluginAdd / pluginRemove / pluginTest , and backend: 'external' tabs have all been removed). Legacy data from older versions is handled on startup: manifests in userData/cli-plugins/external/ are deleted; backend: 'external' tabs are no longer restored (along with their messages and resume files); sidebar sessions bound to those tabs are removed when the tab is closed; a stored external CLI selection in the view falls back to the first agent, and any remaining backend: 'external' records fall back to Nomi as an invalid backend. Protocol details live inside the drivers; per-CLI differences (stream event parsing, history transcripts, model catalogs, slash-command layouts) live inside each plugin. The orchestrator branches on manifest capability flags rather than CLI names (enforced on the view side by the ESLint rule nomi/no-cli-literal , with an allowlist in scripts/eslint/cli-literal-allowlist.mjs ). # Built-in Agent Registry Single source of truth for data : Declarative metadata for every built-in CLI lives in packages/cli-catalog/src/ id /manifest.ts — capability flags, transport, executables and npm package, permission mode - native mode mappings, display name and fullName , config file path ( configPath ), and core runtime metadata ( host : minimum Node version, self-update method, official vendor, ACP launch args, plan follow-up, whether a nomi- id command exists). UI and list ordering is defined by BUILTIN_CLI_ORDER . The Go core reads internal/cliplugins/catalog/catalog.json generated from it ( pnpm -F @nomi-ai/cli-catalog gen:go ; tests/go-catalog.test.ts verifies it is up to date) rather than maintaining a hand-written Go manifest. Go registers code only : internal/cliplugins/ id / implements the main-process logic ( CreateMain() : official/third-party launch, account catalog, slash commands, etc.), and builtin.entries registers it along with transcript parsing. Everything in the core that needs per-CLI handling reads from internal/cliplugins/builtin : Need Source Which built-in CLIs exist builtin.IDs (sorted by ID), builtin.Ordered (UI and list order) Plugin capabilities (permissions, accounts, history, slash commands, terminal, etc.) builtin.Impl(id) (each plugin's CreateMain() , instantiated once) Display name builtin.DisplayName ( Gemini ), builtin.FullName ( Gemini CLI : Agent Board, Usage, Dynamic Island) Manifest capability flags, transport, executables, npm package builtin.Capability , builtin.UsesAcp , builtin.Binaries , builtin.NpmPackage Manifest host section builtin.MinNode , SelfUpdate , Vendor , AcpArgs , PlanFollowUp , NomiCommand Capability-filtered lists builtin.Where(builtin.WithAccounts / WithHistory / WithQuota / WithThirdParty / LocalOnly / All) Views use BUILTIN_CLI_ORDER , cliCapability , cliName , cliFullName , cliConfigPath , and byCli from @nomi-ai/cli-catalog . Permission capabilities for ACP agents are derived from the manifest ( shared.AcpPermissions ) rather than duplicated in Go. Two guard tests block hardcoded lists (3 or more built-in IDs on one line or across adjacent lines): internal/cliplugins/builtin/hardcoded_test.go on the Go side and packages/cli-catalog/tests/no-hardcoded-lists.test.ts on the view side. Implementations that genuinely apply only to specific CLIs (quota queries, usage log parsing, brand icons, gateway client entries) are registered in the test allowlists with an explicit reason. builtin_test.go verifies a one-to-one correspondence between code entries and manifests, and that manifest history flags match the implementation. Adding a built-in agent (using ACP as an example): packages/cli-catalog/src/ id / : add manifest.ts and renderer.ts ; append to BUILTIN_CLI_ORDER ; run gen:ids and gen:go . apps/desktop-go/internal/cliplugins/ id / : add manifest.go (two lines: pulled from catalog) and CreateMain() ; register in builtin.entries . Add the brand icon ( packages/ui/src/brand/endpointGlyphs.ts and the copy in the Dynamic Island page), English/Chinese i18n strings, and documentation. Lists, display names, detection, installation and updates, Agent Board process recognition, delegation, ACP launch, and settings pages will all pick it up automatically; add quota queries or usage log parsing in their respective places if needed. Third-party models: set thirdParty: true in the manifest, and have the plugin implement Launch.ThirdParty , returning a private home directory ( PrivateHome : environment variables and unlinked entries) and config files to write ( Files ). gwstore/agents.AgentLaunchFor calls it for CLIs without a dedicated handler, creates the private home directory, and writes the files ( 0600 ). CLIs without a dedicated gateway entry use the generic entry ( clients.GenericSpec : lenient validation, mapping unknown model names to the primary model). The model is written into the config file; switching models restarts the process and resumes via session/load . nomi- cli commands in the terminal require launch script support (manifest host.nomiCommand ). # Projects A project ( internal/core/projects , userData/projects.json , contract project.* / project.changed ) is a named group of folders: primary is the primary folder and folders holds additional folders. The model aligns with ACP's Additional Directories : cwd remains the primary directory and anchor for relative paths, while additional folders expand read/write scope; git, worktrees, and AGENTS.md look only at the primary folder. Sessions store only projectId : Nomi chats store it in conversation metadata, and agents store it in the tab object ( tabs.json ). Paths are never persisted in sessions; every time they are used, Store.Roots(id) fetches them live and re-validates them against workspace root rules: if the primary folder is unavailable, the whole project is unavailable; if an additional folder is unavailable, it is skipped. Nomi : desktop.ApplyConversationWorkspace resolves desktop.Workspace from extra.projectId and rewrites extra.cwd to the primary folder (discarding any path supplied by the view). File tools re-resolve via ExecContext.ProjectID on each call ( PermissionBroker.WorkspaceOf ), with guard scopes covering all folders ( Workspace.Scopes ). Agents : The working directory is the primary folder (except for delegated worktree tabs). Additional folders are fetched on each launch by Orchestrator.extraDirs : --add-dir for Claude Code, per-turn sandboxPolicy.writableRoots for Codex app-server ( -c sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots for exec fallback), --include-directories for Gemini, and session/new / session/load for other ACP agents declaring sessionCapabilities.additionalDirectories ; Nomi's OS sandbox also adds them as writable directories. When a project changes ( Store.OnChange - Orchestrator.ProjectChanged ), idle tabs disconnect persistent processes and restart with the new folders on the next turn while resuming the same session; if the primary folder changed, the working directory updates and prior context is carried over.
