If a file is outside the session's working directory but inside one of a project's folders (another folder of the same project or another project), the core fetches that project's currently available folders via resourcepreview.Service.ProjectRoots and picks the deepest matching folder as an editable root without requiring per-file authorization. Files outside all projects still require user confirmation and open read-only once confirmed. Migration : migrateToProjects creates single-folder projects from each conversation metadata cwd , tab directory, and background task directory, and updates sessions to reference projectId . It runs whenever projects.json does not exist or userData/projects-migration.pending remains (from an interrupted run); every step is idempotent, and the marker is removed only after full completion. Only conversations successfully migrated drop cwd ; conversations whose directories are currently unavailable (unmounted external drive, offline network share) retain cwd and retry on subsequent launches. # Permission Modes Manifest modes: plan , manual , acceptEdits , auto , bypass ( packages/cli-catalog/src/manifest.ts ). Each CLI maps them to its own launch flags or session mode ( session/set_mode in ACP). Tool calls requiring confirmation enter the orchestrator's permission queue ( permissionqueue.go ) and are answered in the view; replies can be multi-option (allow once / this session / deny). Structured questions do not enter the permission queue; they go through internal/core/askuser question cards (above the chat input bar, 10-minute timeout): Claude Code's AskUserQuestion , Codex app-server's item/tool/requestUserInput , Codex's form-based mcpServer/elicitation/request , and ACP's elicitation/create (advertising elicitation.form during handshake). Answers, skips, cancellations, and timeouts are written back in each protocol's native format. When Codex wraps an MCP tool approval as an elicitation ( codex_approval_kind: mcp_tool_call ), it still routes through allow/deny; URL elicitations are cancelled immediately. Codex's exec fallback has no interactive back-channel. MCP servers connected directly by Nomi do not advertise elicitation and do not enter this card. # Sources and Tab Tokens Official : The CLI uses an official account managed by Nomi (each account has an isolated config directory, and login is performed by the CLI itself; see accounts/ ). Local login is no longer supported: built-in agents do not use the machine's default CLI login directory; agents without official account support ( dsh , Gemini) only have third-party sources. Legacy local- kind records are deleted on read, and tabs or default for new sessions preferences pointing to them switch to follow the default official account. Third-party : The CLI points to the local unified gateway. Before launch, the orchestrator issues a nomi-tab- token and registers a binding (tab, generation, model, thinking depth), waiting for confirmation before starting the process. Switching models or third-party providers re-registers the binding and takes effect on the next turn. Official account sign-in: Codex uses device code flow — once the UI receives the sign-in URL and device code, it automatically opens the browser only once. Grok uses the grok login --oauth browser callback flow, where the CLI opens the browser. The sign-in modal does not inherit the settings page's embedded mode and only responds to an active sign-in initiated from the current page that has not been closed; late events arriving after close do not reopen the modal, and launch responses do not overwrite earlier sign-in progress. # Subtasks (Tabs Delegated by Nomi) Subtask drawer ( packages/ai-chat/src/components/SubagentPane , state in contexts/SubagentPaneContext ): the main column stays on the source conversation. Delegated tabs use CliConversation + MessageInput , calling sendToTab / replyPermissionFor / cancelRun by tab ID without calling activate . In-process subagents show steps from the parent transcript whose parentId points to them; delegate_to_nomi renders tasks.trace . See docs/design/subagent-chat-parity.md for design details. Takeover: sending a message while a delegation is actively running counts as taking over (interrupting Nomi's turn, delegation.takenOver ); sending while idle simply continues the conversation without marking a takeover. Reporting: TabFinished.Origin records who initiated the turn ( user / sandbox / programmatic). Turns sent by the user or resumed after sandbox authorization are handed by coding_wiring.go to delegate.ReportFollowUp , returning to the source conversation via delegate.completed ( followUp: true ); delegation's own turns are reported by finalize . # Local Protection Working directory policies, environment variable scrubbing, Codex network disabled by default, OS-level sandboxing, and per-session grants: see security.md Agents . # Testing Mock CLIs live in scripts/mock-cli/mock- cli .mjs at the repo root. When NOMI_USE_MOCK_CLI=1 , cli.MockCliBin searches upward from the current directory for scripts/mock-cli (so it works even when pnpm dev runs from apps/desktop-go ) and uses them in place of real CLIs. If the file is missing, the CLI is treated as not installed. Unit tests for the orchestrator, drivers, and plugins live in their respective packages ( go test ./internal/core/cli/... ./internal/clisdk/... ./internal/cliplugins/... ). Subprocess tests wait on explicit conditions (with descriptive timeouts) rather than counting polling iterations.

d: Path grants, command review, code sandbox, network and keys
x: For user-facing documentation, see features/privacy-security.md ; this page lists the implementation locations—review them before modifying these subsystems. # Views ⇄ Core Views access the core exclusively through the app contract ( contract.md ): each window receives a one-time token by which the core identifies the caller's surface; surfaces and dangerous on each procedure are enforced by the guard in internal/contract/frames.go . The WebSocket listens only on 127.0.0.1 . Native paths of dropped files are obtained by the host from native drag-and-drop events ( WindowFilesDropped in wailsshell ); views cannot submit arbitrary paths. Views pass only a project ID ( extra.projectId for Nomi chat, projectId for new tabs), never a directory path: project folders are fetched live by the core from core/projects , re-validated against workspace root rules before every use, and treated as absent if unrecognized; any extra.cwd supplied by a view is discarded. # Desktop Capabilities (Nomi's File / Command Tools) apps/desktop-go/internal/core/desktop : File Role path_guard.go Authorized scopes + blocklist + path normalization + realpath check against symlink escapes workspace.go Project folders ( Workspace : primary folder + additional folders) as implicit read/write scopes; rejects overly broad roots (home directory, drive roots, etc.) protected_paths.go User's protected folders (stored as realpath ) and env vars allowlisted for agents; CheckCliWorkspace applies the same rules to agent tab working directories permission_broker.go , consent.go Authorization scopes, tool policies, confirmation prompts, cloud outbound consent; determines when user confirmation is required command_class.go Deterministic command classification (credential reads, irreversible actions, external side effects) command_review.go Sends workspace_run commands to an auxiliary model for risk assessment: low-risk commands proceed, uncertain/high-risk commands prompt the user (card shows risk level and reason); never silently blocks on the user's behalf. Secrets/tokens and the home directory are redacted before sending to the review model; the review card and settings explicitly disclose that the full command text is sent. command_rules.go Command allowlist: strictly allowlist-based, accepting only program + subcommand pairs in ruleSubcommands and inspection tools in ruleProgramsAlone ; dangerous flags ( unsafeRuleArgs ) and classes in command_class.go are never eligible; bypassed after reading external content in the current turn, after writing files while tainted (paused until the user manually confirms a command), in manual mode, or under an explicit ask policy outbound_guard.go Blocks or substitutes attachment contents and agent output according to settings before sending to cloud models audit_log.go Desktop tool call audit log ( desktop-YYYY-MM.jsonl , arguments redacted) undo_journal.go Inverse operation journal for undoable actions # Agents (CLI Subprocesses) Agents run as the current user. Nomi enforces the following protections in internal/core/cli/harness , regardless of permission mode: Working directory : Deps.CwdCheck (wired to desktop.PermissionBroker.CheckCliWorkspace , sharing the same rules as Nomi chat workspaces: must not be overly broad and must not lie inside built-in or user-protected folders). Checked when creating a tab, changing directories, and before every CLI launch ( cwdErr in spawn.go ). Additional project folders : Tabs store only projectId ; additional folders are fetched live from core/projects on every launch (validated against workspace root rules when creating/editing a project, and re-checked on fetch) and passed to the CLI ( --add-dir / writableRoots / additionalDirectories ), with the same write access as the working directory inside the OS sandbox (read-only in plan mode). See coding-agents.md Projects . Environment variables : CliChildEnv first runs cli.ScrubSecretEnv ( internal/core/cli/envscrub.go ) to strip inherited credential variables (tokens, passwords, cloud access keys, connection strings), except model service credentials and user-allowlisted variables ( Deps.EnvAllow ); variables injected by Nomi itself (tab tokens, official account directories) are preserved. Nomi's workspace_run uses the same environment ( desktopShellEnv in igtools_wiring.go ). Codex network access : codexNetwork defaults to off, persisted under codexNetworkAllowed (true only if explicitly enabled by the user). The approval policy for acceptEdits is on-request , so out-of-sandbox requests trigger Codex approval prompts routed into the permission queue. (When Nomi's OS sandbox is active, Codex's own sandbox is disabled and this setting has no effect; see below.) # OS-Level Sandbox (macOS) Threat model : The sandbox defends against agent accidental misuse and prompt-injection exfiltration or corruption (reading credentials, modifying user configs, writing outside the project). It does not stop a determined malicious process: it is a default-allow + deny-by-path blocklist without network restrictions, so everything else a process can do (spawning subprocesses, connecting to remote services) still works. Risk reduction comes from denying reads to sensitive data, scrubbing environment variables, restricting writable locations, and closing the bypass vectors listed below; stronger isolation (containers, VMs) is out of scope here. internal/core/cli/sandbox + harness/sandbox.go . Every session process (Claude persistent process, Codex app-server / exec, ACP, per-turn CLI processes) is wrapped with /usr/bin/sandbox-exec -p profile ( spawnCLI - spawnHarness ), with profiles generated per tab and per launch ( sandbox.Profile ): Default allow, with read-data denied ( file-read-data ; directory listing and stat remain allowed) by category: SSH and Git credentials (including GitHub CLI tokens), cloud account credentials (including .pypirc / .gem/credentials publish tokens in the home directory), secrets and password vaults (including 1Password CLI's .config/op ), browser data (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave, Arc, Chromium, Vivaldi, Opera, Safari), personal data (Mail / Messages / Calendar / Contacts / Notes / Photos, plus shell and REPL histories), secret files ( .env* excluding .env.example etc., *.key , private .pem keys, etc. in the home directory and project), plus user-protected folders and Nomi's own data directory (except prompt-images and CLI official account directories). The system Keychain is not blocked: blocking Keychain reads breaks official CLI sign-ins, and items are already protected by macOS access controls. ~/.pypirc in the home directory is still read-denied, but treated as a routine package manager read ( RoutineRead ) without popping an authorization prompt. ~/.npmrc is readable but not writable: it often configures registry mirrors, and denying reads causes sandboxed npm to hit the default registry or causes nvm to error on every shell startup; writes remain blocked ( write:config , since script-shell , node-options , etc. can execute commands via npm outside the sandbox). Writes allowed: project directories (except in plan mode), temp directories, /dev , the CLI's own directories (manifest host.homeDirs : ~/.claude , ~/.codex , ~/.kimi-code , ~/.minimax , ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli , ..., plus ~/.claude.json* ) and account / third-party private directories pointed to by host.homeEnv , package manager and build caches ( ~/Library/Caches , ~/.npm , go/pkg , ...), tool state (hidden entries directly under home ~/.* , ~/.config , ~/Library/Application Support , toolStateHome : where tools write logs, caches, and state—such as hook scripts writing ~/.ai-usage —without prompting for authorization), and user-authorized folders/files. Regular directories under home (Documents, Desktop, Downloads, code directories outside the project) require authorization before writing. Post-allow denials: unauthorized credential-category folders and top-level home credential files ( ~/.ssh , ~/.aws , ~/.netrc , ..., rule write , which still trigger authorization prompts); files whose modification executes commands outside the sandbox (rule write:config , no authorization prompt): CLI hooks and configs ( execConfigHome and manifest host.execConfig : ~/.claude/settings.json , ~/.claude/hooks , ~/.codex/config.toml , ~/.gemini/settings.json , ~/.kimi-code/config.toml , ~/.minimax/config.yaml , ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json ), configs executed by other tools on startup ( homeExecConfig : ~/.config/git , Vim/Neovim, tmux, Hammerspoon, yarn/bun/curl configs, direnv, Cursor/Windsurf/Claude Desktop MCP configs, VS Code / Cursor user settings, ...), login-item/autostart directories, executable directories in PATH , shell startup scripts, and ~/.gitconfig ; protected folders and Nomi's data directory are denied again last. Local escape vectors : Unix sockets are not governed by file read/write rules, so outbound connections ( network-outbound remote unix-socket ) are blocked explicitly: ssh-agent ( /private/var/run/com.apple.launchd.*/Listeners , agent.sock , S.gpg-agent ) is blocked unless the SSH category is authorized, and SSH_AUTH_SOCK is stripped from the environment; Docker's docker.sock (Docker Desktop, Colima, OrbStack) is blocked unless the cloud-accounts category is authorized. Apple Events ( appleevent-send ) are always denied so osascript cannot drive Terminal or Finder outside the sandbox. Denials for these vectors are logged only. Seatbelt cannot be nested (inner sandbox_apply fails when outer deny rules exist), so CLIs have their own sandboxes disabled when wrapped: Claude --settings { sandbox :{ enabled :false}} , Codex dangerFullAccess / sandbox_mode= danger-full-access (approval policy stays intact), Gemini GEMINI_SANDBOX=false , dsh DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access . Network access is unrestricted (Seatbelt only filters by IP, and CLIs must reach model services); exfiltration is mitigated via sensitive-read denials and env scrubbing. Every denial carries (with message nomi-sbx: token : rule ) . sandbox.Monitor reads violations via log stream --predicate 'sender == Sandbox AND eventMessage CONTAINS nomi-sbx: ' (readable by unprivileged users, including process, operation, and realpath), matches the token back to the tab, and sandbox.Classify maps it to an authorization request: category, write to a folder (minimal scope: the file's parent directory, bounded by the git repo root if inside one, never opening up broad folders like ~/Projects ), write to a specific file (when the parent folder is too broad, such as files directly in home), read of a specific secret file ( .env etc. are authorized per file rather than opening the whole category), or protected folder (cannot be authorized in chat). Never grantable for writes ( sandbox.NeverGrantable , no authorization prompt): autostart locations ( ~/Library/LaunchAgents , /Library/LaunchAgents , /Library/LaunchDaemons ), executable directories in PATH ( ~/.local/bin , ~/bin , /usr/local/bin , /opt/homebrew/bin , ~/go/bin , ~/.cargo/bin , ~/.bun/bin , ~/.deno/bin ), and shell configs ( ~/.oh-my-zsh , ~/.zsh , fish/zsh config dirs, ~/.zshrc and other startup scripts, ~/.gitconfig ). When parsing violations, the message must consist strictly of one denial line + one tag line, paths cannot contain control characters, and a mismatched token forged via a filename inside the sandbox is discarded. Denials on Nomi's data directory are logged only. New requests also emit permission-needed (triggering a desktop character bubble and system notification when background is true). Pending requests sit on tab state sandboxPending (not persisted; each item is queued only once) and are shown on the agent tab, delegation card, and task details. harness.sandboxReply handles responses: allow for this session (in tab memory), always allow (desktop setting cliSandboxAllow : each entry carries project = realpath of the working directory's git root, scoped solely to that project, matched by realpath so symlinked working directories cannot borrow another project's grants; validated on both load and insertion for valid category, absolute path, non-broad folder, and non-never-grantable path), or deny (do not ask again in this session). After allowing, recycleTab retires the tab's old CLI process (waiting for the current turn if running); the next user message launches a new process with updated permissions and resumes the session. Granting permission only updates permissions—it does not send please continue on the user's behalf or auto-start a new turn, and a stopped session will not resume solely because a grant was approved. Task pre-authorization: task-authorized grant.sandbox (category IDs), automatically including ssh when GitHub outbound capabilities are present ( tasks.SandboxGrants ), are written into delegation.sandboxGrants on tab creation and treated as already granted in grantedFor . Only the core's internal delegation/task paths may set delegation : the harness.tabCreate contract procedure accepts only view-provided fields ( backend , cwd , title , messages , permissionMode ) and discards internal fields such as delegation . Informing the agent it is sandboxed ( prompts/text/cli-sandbox.md ): Claude receives it via --append-system-prompt , while other CLIs receive it prepended to the first message of the CLI session ( withSandboxNote ). If blocked, the agent should stop, explain, and end the turn rather than working around it. The note also states that the CLI's own config directories (skills, prompts, plugins) and ~/.agents are readable and executable, and that Permission denied / exit code 126 when running a script indicates a missing executable bit rather than a sandbox block (sandbox blocks produce Operation not permitted ), so the agent should invoke the script via an interpreter and continue instead of stopping ( internal/core/cli/sandbox/skills_test.go guards the skill directories of every built-in CLI). Policy changes: toggling cliSandboxOff (sandbox enabled by default), protected folders, or always allow entries triggers watchSandboxPolicy - SandboxPolicyChanged , restarting idle persistent CLIs with the updated profile. On other platforms, sandbox.Supported() is false and CLIs run as before (status unsupported , surfaced in the UI); working directory checks and environment scrubbing still apply. When no OS sandbox is available, normal (non-delegated) L3 background tasks do not switch to auto : the agent permission mode stays at acceptEdits (file edits proceed automatically, commands still require confirmation), and both risk-based auto-approval and foreground auto-approve all continue prompting per command (never silently carry over macOS auto-execution to Windows/Linux). For subagents delegated from Nomi chat , both synchronous and background delegations use DelegatePermissionMode(cli) —the highest mode supported by that CLI (typically bypass )—and the approval confirmation card must explicitly display the actual permission mode along with the active host protections (OS sandbox on/off/unsupported, working directory validation, and env scrubbing). # Code Execution Sandbox apps/desktop-go/internal/core/sandbox : Language / Platform Isolation Fallback JavaScript Native node --permission , read/write restricted to temp dir, code-generation-from-strings disabled, memory-capped — Python · macOS sandbox-exec + built-in Seatbelt profile (writes restricted to temp dir, network disabled by default) Binary not found - bare python -I Python · Linux bwrap (read-only system dirs, writable temp dir, --unshare-net ) bubblewrap not installed - bare python -I Python · Windows No filesystem isolation — The sandbox field in the result indicates which isolation mode actually ran, and the UI surfaces it accordingly; stricter confirmation is required when isolation is absent. # Delegation Working Directory When Nomi delegates tasks to an agent via delegate_to_cli (or persistent task agent execution) ( internal/core/cli/delegate/ ): By default, edits run in-place in the working directory without creating a worktree. Parallel tasks in the same git repository register which files they are modifying ( claims.go , derived from file-editing tool event inputs). When two tasks touch the same file, priority arbitrates ( urgent high medium low , first-come wins on ties): the yielding task receives a steer message telling it not to touch that file again; at wrap-up, the file counts toward the winning task, and files edited by concurrent tasks are excluded from one's own change list. Files modified via shell commands cannot be attributed from tool args, so unclaimed files listed by git still count as the task's own. A detached worktree under cwd /.nomi-delegate/ id is created only when a distinct base_branch not in the current branch's history is explicitly specified ( .nomi-delegate/ is added to the repo's info/exclude ). Landing a worktree ( LandWorktree ): small changes ( = 10 files and = 400 lines) are copied back to the active working tree, skipping target files that already have uncommitted changes or lie outside authorized scope; larger changes or uncopiable files are committed to a new branch nomi/ base - id (no hooks, no signing) for the user to decide whether to merge. Commits made directly by the agent that are not referenced by any branch or tag (a clean git status does not mean no work was done) also get a branch created to preserve them. The worktree is removed after landing; if preserving fails (inspection or branch creation error), the worktree is kept and an error is reported. Synchronous delegations land immediately upon completion; persistent tasks land via Land Changes on the acceptance card or automatically when accepted. On cancellation, failure/abandonment, expiration, or task deletion, the worktree is removed (except for tabs taken over by the user). On app startup, unclaimed delegation worktrees are cleaned up: uncommitted changes are committed to a new branch and unreferenced commits receive a branch before removal; if that fails, the worktree is preserved. Non-git directories run in-place, and the result warns that parallel tasks may overwrite each other's files. The combined concurrency limit for active delegations and background tasks is governed by the Agent Board's scheduling policy (Eco: 5 / Balanced: 10 / Full Speed: resource-gated; defaults to 3 delegations via MaxParallelDelegates if the board is not initialized). Each agent's built-in sandbox (such as Codex's Seatbelt) still applies normally; this layer solely prevents concurrent writes to the same working tree. Delegated agent tabs are visible only inside Nomi (subtask cards in chat, the subtask drawer beside chat, and the Tasks page): they do not appear in the sidebar, and their sessions do not appear in the agent's history ( harness/orchestrator_delegated.go ). Identical delegations in the same conversation (matching agents, directory, task type, model, and thinking depth) reuse the previous idle session (if used within the last hour, reuse.go ) to save tokens and startup time; worktree delegations are never reused. Delegated tabs whose associated tasks have finished and that have been idle for over a week are closed on app startup (since users cannot close them from the sidebar). # Network Outbound URLs allow only public http(s) endpoints, rejecting embedded credentials and reserved addresses ( internal/core/security/netguard.go ). Gateway outbound traffic also enforces address classification and DNS IP pinning ( internal/gateway/net ) to prevent post-resolution DNS rebinding to private networks. Both the gateway and contract servers listen strictly on loopback addresses and validate the Host header. # Secrets and Privacy Secrets such as API keys: a master key is stored in the OS keychain and encrypted enc: values are persisted on disk ( internal/core/security/secretbox.go ); if the keychain is unavailable, it fails closed rather than falling back to plaintext. Privacy mode: the gateway substitutes secrets, tokens, and other sensitive strings with placeholders before sending requests upstream and restores them in responses ( internal/gateway/privacy ). Diagnostic logs and audit records are redacted before writing ( internal/core/services/redact.go , audit_log.go ).

Raising them is always fine; lowering them requires an explanation in the PR. For UI flows that schedule delayed requests (such as local history mounting after 120 ms), enable vi.useFakeTimers() in the test so untilIdle flushes scheduled timers on each pass. Existing test files still contain many waitFor calls—replace them as you touch those files. Waiting on subprocesses or asynchronous disk writes must wait on explicit conditions (with descriptive timeouts) rather than counting fixed polling iterations or asserting wall-clock elapsed time. CI runs apps/desktop-go/ci/go-test.sh : go vet first, then go test -race . Failing packages are retried once; passing on the second attempt is flagged as flaky ( ::warning:: + job summary), while failing twice fails the job. d: Rules for UI strings and translations
x: Nomi's localization resources are centralized in the @nomi-ai/i18n package ( packages/i18n ); views, the Go core, and plugins all share the same dictionary. packages/ui only retains locale state and view bindings; the Go core embeds a copy ( apps/desktop-go/internal/core/i18n/locales , verified against the source by dict_test.go ) and resolves strings via i18n.T(key, args...) . At runtime, only stable keys ( project.module.message ) are resolved— raw Chinese text cannot be used as a key , and there is no automatic fallback mapping. # Keys and Directory Layout Stable keys use three-segment lowercase kebab-case: project.module.message . Directory Purpose src/locales/zh Baseline Chinese dictionary defining the canonical key set src/locales/en English dictionary src/locales/ language Additional languages, named with short language codes such as ja src/locales/ language / project Project boundary, e.g., ui , electron (legacy name kept for core/main-process strings), ai-runtime *.json Module dictionary, e.g., chat-settings.json , common.json Every key must exist in zh and all enabled languages, and interpolation placeholders such as {0} or {name} must match across languages. Within the same project, two keys must not share identical baseline text, preventing ambiguity during maintenance and translation checks. Dictionaries hold UI copy only. Prompts sent to models do not belong in dictionaries; they live in internal/core/prompts/text in the Go core (see apps/desktop-go/README.md ). Application code always references stable keys: # Workflow for Changes Add or update the key in the same module across zh and all other languages. Run node scripts/i18n/refresh-catalog.mjs to update the generated catalog.ts . If you modified keys also used by Go (such as electron or ai-runtime ), run pnpm i18n:sync to sync packages/i18n/src/locales byte-for-byte to apps/desktop-go/internal/core/i18n/locales (TS is the single source of truth—never copy manually; pnpm check:i18n passes --check and fails CI on drift). Run pnpm check:i18n . Run typecheck and tests for affected packages (Go: go test ./internal/core/i18n/ ). The check reports: Chinese keys, invalid key formats, missing or extra translations, mismatched placeholders, duplicate baseline text within a project, unknown keys in source code, and dead keys. String literals in Go source and embedded JSON ( apps/desktop-go , excluding tests) are also counted as usages ( goKeySources ); format strings like fmt.Sprintf( electron.common.task-level-%d , n) match a group of keys by pattern; keys under electron.* or ai-runtime.* referenced in Go but absent from the dictionary are reported as unknown. # keepZh (Retaining Chinese) keepZh in scripts/i18n/config.cjs lists source files that intentionally retain Chinese text outside the dictionary . These strings are used for model prompts or internal parsing rather than user-facing UI: Wake words ( voice/src/wake.ts ) Model prompts and tool schemas in the Go core do not go through the dictionary; the checker inspects Go files only for strings shaped like stable keys and ignores Chinese prose inside them. Do not use keepZh to bypass checks for user-facing UI strings; put them in packages/i18n and call t() / tr() . Update this document whenever keepZh is modified.

d: Tokens, components and styling rules
x: These standards apply to packages/ui , packages/ai-chat , and packages/renderer . The goal is to let components, state, styles, and copy evolve independently while reducing regression risk across desktop windows. These rules serve as the default baseline for code review; any exception must be documented near the code and registered in the exceptions section of this file. # Directory and Dependency Boundaries All UI icons must use named imports from @tabler/icons-react , controlling size and stroke width primarily through the shared Icon component; namespace imports of the whole library, dynamic icon-name lookups, and runtime icon services are forbidden. Icones is only for searching and picking icons—do not import its runtime. Provider and agent product logos use shared BrandIcon / EndpointIcon , while Nomi keeps its own brand assets. From LobeHub, store only the static SVGs actually in use; update them via scripts/icons/update-brands.mjs , which also regenerates Dynamic Island assets, then format the generated files with Prettier. packages/ui contains only cross-window design tokens and business-agnostic components with no business state or host dependencies. Components must be exported via packages/ui/src/index.ts ; pages must never import from internal paths inside the UI package. packages/ai-chat and packages/renderer organize pages by feature. A feature folder may contain index.tsx , local subcomponents, hooks, services, and CSS Modules; code shared across features moves up to packages/ui or the package's shared directory. Dependencies remain strictly unidirectional: ui - React/icon library , feature packages - ui/types/sdk-client , and views communicate with the Go core solely through the app contract ( services/api.ts ). The UI package must never depend on feature packages or window implementations. Page components handle composition and routing, presentational/feature components handle rendering and interaction, hooks handle state and side effects, services handle IPC/API adaptation, and pure logic lives in utils . Components must never assemble IPC channel names directly. Top-bar panel tools reuse the original components via slots in TitleBar/panels.tsx , preserving panel state inside those components. Column boundaries in the desktop window use ResizeObserver to measure actual panel widths, while the browser preview retains the in-panel toolbar. The splash screen manages only the visual overlay and exits once the conversation index, initial messages, and first-frame layout are ready; it must never modify onboarding completion flags or conversation data. # Files, Components, and Shared Capabilities Source files ( .ts , .tsx , .css , .json ) must not exceed 1,200 lines by default. Beyond that, split by responsibility into separate files for page composition, presentational components, state hooks, service adapters, and pure functions. Exceptions are permitted only for tightly coupled rendering engines, generated protocol artifacts, or external data files that cannot be safely split by responsibility; each must document its reason, owner, and future split criteria. Individual React components must not exceed 300 lines by default; past 200 lines, check whether a component is mixing data fetching, state machines, and layout composition. UI patterns that repeat twice with stable semantics should be extracted into packages/ui . Shared components must support keyboard navigation, focus states, disabled states, and accessible names, and be exported from index.ts . Pages must not duplicate foundational interactive structures such as Button , Modal , FormField , EmptyState , or SectionTitle ; add explicit props or variants on shared components instead of overriding or building parallel implementations in feature layers. useEffect is restricted to subscriptions, timers, external APIs, and DOM/IPC synchronization. Derived values are computed during render; async requests must guard against cancellation or stale responses. # Styling and Theming Shared components use var(--cd-*) tokens and the cd- class prefix; feature-specific styles use CSS Modules. Never scatter hardcoded colors, spacing, radii, or shadows. Split shared CSS by responsibility so the entry file contains only @import statements; base components, theme overrides, and complex controls must not be mixed in one long file. Interactive states must cover hover , focus-visible , disabled , and reduced-motion (where applicable). Modals must support Esc to close, focus restoration, and screen-reader titles. Menus, popovers, and drawers should not unmount immediately on close: use usePresence(value) from @nomi-ai/ui to play the exit animation first (it returns the previous value and closing , setting data-closing on the element), paired with global classes cd-motion-pop (menus: fade and gentle drop) or cd-motion-slide-right (right-side overlays: slide in from right and fade in), reversing on close; unmount immediately when reduced motion is enabled. Keep the value passed to usePresence referentially stable across renders (a stateful object, boolean, or string—never construct a fresh object every render). # Accessibility and Tooltips Never add native title attributes to icon buttons, including buttons that collapse to icon-only states. Provide an explicit accessible name with aria-label ; shared IconButton takes label and does not accept a title prop. Prefer visible copy or inline expansion for explanations; when hover explanations are needed, use Tooltip or FloatingTip from @nomi-ai/ui with keyboard focus and Esc dismissal. Keyboard shortcuts must never be conveyed solely via hover tooltips. Truncated text may keep a native title attribute to show the full string (such as filenames, paths, model IDs, or timestamps), which installTitleTooltips() intercepts and renders as a custom styled tooltip. The title prop used for visible headings in Modal , SettingRow , EmptyState , etc. is unaffected. Meaningful standalone static icons use role= img + aria-label ; decorative icons accompanied by equivalent text use aria-hidden to avoid duplicate announcements. # Internationalization User-facing copy uses stable project.module.message keys via t() / tr() ; logs, model prompts, protocol fields, and parsed data must be explicitly configured as exceptions in the i18n check setup. Dictionaries are centralized in packages/i18n/src/locales/ language / project / module .json with zh as the baseline language. Add new copy to the matching project/module file—never create locale files inside feature packages or manually edit the generated catalog.ts . Interpolation placeholders must stay consistent between zh and all other languages; update all languages together when editing keys and run pnpm check:i18n . Never cache translated strings inside components. Language changes trigger re-renders via useLocale ; dynamic strings must also go through the translation function. # Performance and Testing Lazy-load panels and heavy dependencies by feature; Rive scenes, charts, and editors must stay out of the initial shared chunk. Lists use stable keys and virtualization or pagination; event listeners, IPC subscriptions, animation frames, and object URLs must be released in cleanup functions. Shared components are tested for behavior and accessibility, feature components for key state transitions, and pure functions for edge cases. Tests must never depend on real network access, system clock, or unisolated userData . Before committing, run at least typecheck , lint , and test for affected packages; for cross-package changes, also run root pnpm test , pnpm typecheck , and pnpm build . # Review Checklist Are dependency directions and shared component boundaries clean? Are files and components within line-count budgets, and are any exceptions justified? Is there duplicated interaction logic, duplicated styling, or an unextracted stable pattern? Are loading, empty, error, disabled, keyboard, focus, and reduced-motion states complete? Are icon buttons named strictly via aria-label with no native title ? Is copy placed in the right locale module, with placeholders and English translations in sync? Are side effects cancellable, properly cleaned up, and guarded against stale responses? Have behavioral tests been added and checks passed for affected packages? # Automated Checks and Exceptions Run pnpm check:frontend to verify frontend source line-count budgets; the repo ESLint rule nomi/no-icon-title (under pnpm lint ) blocks native title attributes on icon buttons (see Accessibility and Tooltips ). Currently, the sole registered exception is packages/avatar-runtime/src/layeredRig.ts : it is a tightly coupled Canvas2D animation and rendering engine where splitting would alter rendering order; it will only be decomposed once explicit animation/rendering module boundaries are introduced. All other files exceeding 1,200 lines must be split.
